knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-program reformulation of a local ℓ1 penalty model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific QP representation obtained from a constraint-linearized, curvature-based local ℓ1 penalty model; general ℓ1 penalty stationarity and exactness theory remain outside this statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\), let \(\mu>0\), let \(W=W^T\), and write \(a_i(p)=c_i(x)+\nabla c_i(x)^Tp\). Define
\[
q(p;\mu)=f(x)+\nabla f(x)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TWp+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|a_i(p)|+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[a_i(p)]^-.
\]
For every fixed \(p\), the value \(q(p;\mu)\) equals the minimum over \(r,s,t\geq0\) of
\[
f(x)+\nabla f(x)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TWp+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(r_i+s_i)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i
\]
subject to \(a_i(p)=r_i-s_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(a_i(p)\geq-t_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Hence minimizing \(q\) is representable as a quadratic program. Adding \(\|p\|_\infty\leq\Delta\) adds box constraints and preserves the quadratic-program form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After linearizing each constraint and using a symmetric quadratic curvature model, equality residuals can be split into nonnegative positive and negative parts, while inequality violations can be represented by nonnegative artificial variables. Eliminating those variables recovers the nonsmooth ℓ1 model pointwise, so minimization can be performed as a quadratic program. An infinity-norm trust region only adds box constraints and leaves it a quadratic program.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is fixed while forming the local model}
\Delta\geq0\text{ if the box trust region is imposed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(p;\mu)=\min_{\substack{r,s,t\geq0\\a_i(p)=r_i-s_i\ (i\in\mathcal E)\\a_i(p)\geq-t_i\ (i\in\mathcal I)}}\left[f(x)+\nabla f(x)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TWp+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(r_i+s_i)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i\right],

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic SQP Quadratic Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the quadratic-programming subproblem used by basic SQP. The statement is conditional on the subproblem attaining a minimizer and therefore does not assert feasibility, boundedness, or existence of a search direction. Trust-region and quasi-Newton modifications are optional variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonlinear program with equality constraints indexed by \(\mathcal E\) and inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) indexed by \(\mathcal I\), basic SQP forms at \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) the quadratic subproblem
\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_p\quad &\frac12p^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)p+\nabla f(x_k)^Tp,\\
\text{subject to}\quad &\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp+c_i(x_k)=0, && i\in\mathcal E,\\
&\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp+c_i(x_k)\ge 0, && i\in\mathcal I.
\end{aligned}
\]
If this subproblem attains a minimizer, a minimizer is selected as the search direction \(p_k\). Its constraints are linearizations of the nonlinear constraints. A trust-region constraint may be added, and a quasi-Newton approximation may replace \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the current primal and multiplier estimates, basic sequential quadratic programming forms a quadratic program whose objective combines the objective gradient with Lagrangian curvature and whose constraints linearize the nonlinear equalities and inequalities. When the subproblem has a minimizer, a minimizer defines the search direction. A trust region may be added, and quasi-Newton curvature may replace the exact Lagrangian Hessian.
assumptions_latex: x_k\text{ and }\lambda_k\text{ are the current primal and multiplier estimates}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and consider
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x)=0.\]
At \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\) model Lagrangian curvature. An equality-constrained SQP step is any minimizer of
\[\min_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\; g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kd=0.\]
When \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) for \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\), the objective uses exact Lagrangian curvature and the constraints use their affine first-order model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP step minimizes a quadratic Lagrangian model while satisfying the affine linearization of every equality constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained SQP Models

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained SQP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard SQP model with equalities and one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\quad c(x)\geq0,\]
set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(H_k=\nabla h(x_k)^{\mathsf T}\), and \(C_k=\nabla c(x_k)^{\mathsf T}\). Given \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\), the inequality-constrained SQP model is
\[\min_d\;g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x_k)+H_kd=0,\quad c(x_k)+C_kd\geq0.\]
Thus both constraint families are replaced by their affine first-order models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP subproblem minimizes a quadratic objective subject to affine equality and inequality linearizations.
assumptions_latex: The displayed quadratic program has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k\) solves the displayed linearly constrained quadratic program.

children.top_down_role: SQP subproblems using elastic variables to accommodate difficult constraint models.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic SQP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An ℓ1-elastic reformulation that remains feasible under inconsistent linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given affine models \(r_h(d)=h_k+H_kd\) and \(r_c(d)=c_k+C_kd\), an elastic SQP model introduces \(v,w\in\mathbb R_+^p\) and \(u\in\mathbb R_+^q\):
\[\min_{d,v,w,u}\;g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd+\rho\bigl(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}v+\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w+\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u\bigr)\]
subject to
\[r_h(d)=v-w,\qquad r_c(d)+u\geq0.\]
For every \(d\), suitable nonnegative elastic variables exist; their linear penalty measures affine-constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative elastic variables absorb equality and inequality residuals, ensuring subproblem feasibility while penalizing their total magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic constraint system is feasible, and zero elastic variables recover the ordinary SQP constraints.

notation.meaning: positive and negative equality elastic variables

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_h(d)=h_k+H_kd\) and \(r_c(d)=c_k+C_kd\), where \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r_h(d)\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(r_c(d)\in\mathbb R^q\). A scalar-relaxed SQP model is
\[\min_{d\in\mathbb R^n,\ t\in\mathbb R}\;g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd+\rho t\]
subject to
\[-t\mathbf1_p\leq r_h(d)\leq t\mathbf1_p,\qquad r_c(d)\geq-t\mathbf1_q,\qquad t\geq0.\]
For every \(d\), a sufficiently large \(t\) satisfies these relaxed constraints. Setting \(t=0\) recovers the ordinary affine SQP constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One nonnegative scalar uniformly relaxes all affine constraints and is penalized in the quadratic objective; setting it to zero recovers the unrelaxed constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent-Linearization Recovery Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-recovery model for an empty affine SQP constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(h_k+H_kd=0\) and \(c_k+C_kd\geq0\) are inconsistent, choose \(\Delta>0\) and compute
\[v_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|v\|\leq\Delta}\;\tfrac12\|h_k+H_kv\|_2^2+\tfrac12\|[c_k+C_kv]_-\|_2^2.\]
If the minimum violation is below a prescribed tolerance, use \(v_k\) as a recovered feasibility step or as the normal component of a composite step; otherwise report failure to restore the linearized constraints within radius \(\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the affine constraints conflict, a bounded least-squares model finds the step with smallest combined equality and inequality violation.
assumptions_latex: The negative-part operator is applied componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed \(v_k\) minimizes modeled constraint violation over the trust region.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded least-squares recovery algorithm is plausible and fits the recovery-model leaf, but no citation supports the selected residual norm, trust-region convention, tolerance decision, or use as a composite-step normal component.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Lagrangian Curvature Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Hessian used in the quadratic objective of an SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the Lagrangian
\[L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)-\mu^{\mathsf T}c(x),\]
with inequalities written as \(c(x)\geq0\), the exact SQP curvature matrix at \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\) is
\[B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)=\nabla^2f(x_k)+\sum_i(\lambda_k)_i\nabla^2h_i(x_k)-\sum_j(\mu_k)_j\nabla^2c_j(x_k).\]
The quadratic objective term is \(\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact SQP curvature is the Hessian of the Lagrangian, combining objective and multiplier-weighted constraint Hessians.
assumptions_latex: Equality and inequality multipliers use the displayed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Quasi-Newton SQP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: BFGS Lagrangian-curvature update in the full primal space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and
\[y_k=\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})-\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1}).\]
Starting from \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), if \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), set
\[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^{\mathsf T}B_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^{\mathsf T}}{s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}.\]
Use \(B_{k+1}\) as the full-space quadratic curvature model; if the curvature test fails, apply a specified damping or skip rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space BFGS update approximates the Lagrangian Hessian from successive primal steps and Lagrangian-gradient differences.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is differentiable in \(x\) at both iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian SQP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space representation of equality-constrained SQP curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let the columns of \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker A_k\), and choose \(d_k^p\) satisfying \(A_kd_k^p=-c(x_k)\). Every feasible SQP step has the form \(d=d_k^p+Z_ku\). Substitution gives
\[\min_u\;\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}(Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_k)u+\bigl[Z_k^{\mathsf T}(g_k+B_kd_k^p)\bigr]^{\mathsf T}u,\]
up to terms independent of \(u\). Thus \(Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_k\) is the reduced Hessian model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible particular step plus null-space coordinates converts the equality-constrained SQP model into an unconstrained reduced quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible steps satisfy \(d=d_k^p+Z_ku\), with reduced curvature \(Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search SQP Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP direction generation followed by merit-function line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\), solve the selected SQP quadratic program for a direction \(d_k\). Choose a merit function \(\Phi_\rho\), constants \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), and a predicted directional decrease \(D_k<0\). Select the first \(\alpha_k=\beta^j\), \(j\in\mathbb N_0\), satisfying
\[\Phi_\rho(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq\Phi_\rho(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_kD_k.\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\); multiplier estimates are updated by the specified SQP rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic subproblem supplies a direction, while backtracking selects a step length producing sufficient merit-function decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(d_k\) is obtained from an SQP subproblem.
\(D_k<0\) is a valid predicted merit decrease.
\(\Phi_\rho\) is defined along the trial segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) and satisfies the displayed sufficient-decrease test.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region SQP Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP quadratic model restricted by a bounded step region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an SQP objective model \(q_k(d)=g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\), affine constraint set \(\mathcal F_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and norm \(\|\cdot\|_k\), a trust-region SQP subproblem is
\[\min_{d\in\mathcal F_k}\;q_k(d)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|d\|_k\leq\Delta_k.\]
For equality constraints, \(\mathcal F_k=\{d:c(x_k)+A_kd=0\}\); inequality models may be included analogously. The radius limits the region in which the local models are trusted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region SQP subproblem minimizes the constrained quadratic model while explicitly bounding the trial-step norm.
assumptions_latex: The intersection of \(\mathcal F_k\) with the trust region is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{q_k(d):d\in\mathcal F_k,\ \|d\|_k\leq\Delta_k\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility-restoring formulations of trust-region SQP subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation of trust-region SQP models that address incompatibility between linearized constraints and the trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) and \(I\) index differentiable constraints \(c_i(x)=0\) and \(c_i(x)\ge 0\), respectively, and let \(v(z)_i=z_i\) for \(i\in E\) and \(v(z)_i=\min\{z_i,0\}\) for \(i\in I\). The direct trust-region SQP subproblem minimizes \(g_k^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\) subject to the linearized constraints and \(\|d\|\le\Delta_k\), but these constraints may have an empty intersection. Four modifications are described: (i) replace \(c_i(x_k)\) in the linearized constraints by \(\theta_kc_i(x_k)\), with \(0<\theta_k\le1\); when the linearized system is consistent and \(d_k^{GN}\) denotes its minimum-norm correction, the scaled system intersects the trust region if and only if \(\theta_k\|d_k^{GN}\|\le\Delta_k\). If \(\theta_k<1\), the additional condition \(\theta_k\|d_k^{GN}\|\ge\delta_1\Delta_k\), \(0<\delta_1<1\), avoids unnecessary shrinking; the displayed rule chooses \(\theta_k=1\) when \(2\|d_k^{GN}\|\le\Delta_k\) and \(\theta_k=\Delta_k/(2\|d_k^{GN}\|)\) otherwise. (ii) Treat \(\theta\in(0,1]\) as a variable and add \(\sigma_k(\theta-1)^2\), \(\sigma_k>0\), to the quadratic objective. (iii) impose \(\|v(c_k+A_k^Td)\|_2^2\le\xi_k\) together with \(\|d\|_2\le\Delta_k\); feasibility requires and is ensured by \(\xi_k\ge\min_{\|d\|_2\le\Delta_k}\|v(c_k+A_k^Td)\|_2^2\). The extract gives a Cauchy-step value and a nested-radius interval, with \(1>b_1\ge b_2>0\), as concrete choices of \(\xi_k\). (iv) move the violation into the objective and minimize \(g_k^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd+\sigma_k\|v(c_k+A_k^Td)\|\) subject to \(\|d\|\le\Delta_k\); the violation norm and trust-region norm need not be the same. This last formulation is a nonsmooth trust-region model for \(P(x,\sigma)=f(x)+\sigma\|v(c(x))\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual trust-region SQP quadratic subproblem can be infeasible because its linearized constraints need not intersect the trust region. The extract presents four remedies: scale the constraint residuals, optimize that scaling with a penalty favoring one, bound the least attainable linearized violation, or put the violation directly into an exact-penalty objective. The norm test for the scaled formulation requires consistency of the underlying linearized system. The violation threshold must be at least the minimum attainable violation within the trust region. The exact-penalty formulation may use different norms for violation and step control and is a nonsmooth trust-region model.
assumptions_latex: c_i\text{ is differentiable at }x_k\text{ for every }i\in E\cup I.
\text{The equivalence }\theta_k\|d_k^{GN}\|\le\Delta_k\text{ assumes consistency of the linearized constraint system and that }d_k^{GN}\text{ is its minimum-norm correction}.
0<\theta_k\le1,\quad 0<\delta_1<1,\quad \sigma_k>0\text{ where the corresponding constructions are used}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Incompatibility between the SQP linearization and the trust region can be addressed by residual scaling, penalized scaling, a feasible violation bound, or an exact-penalty trust-region model, under the stated conditions.}

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Step SQP Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-component trust-region SQP step separating feasibility and optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given radius \(\Delta_k>0\), first compute a normal step \(v_k\) that approximately reduces a constraint-violation model subject to \(\|v_k\|\leq\zeta\Delta_k\), where \(0<\zeta<1\). Then compute a correction \(u_k\) by approximately minimizing
\[q_k(v_k+u)=g_k^{\mathsf T}(v_k+u)+\tfrac12(v_k+u)^{\mathsf T}B_k(v_k+u)\]
subject to the chosen tangency conditions and \(\|v_k+u\|\leq\Delta_k\). Output \(d_k=v_k+u_k\), or report failure if either required decrease condition is unmet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite SQP step first improves feasibility and then adds a trust-region-bounded correction aimed at optimality.
assumptions_latex: The normal and tangential subproblems have specified approximate-solution criteria.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial step is \(d_k=v_k+u_k\) with \(\|d_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-stage algorithm fits the composite-step leaf, but no source is supplied and the chosen tangency and required-decrease conditions are left unspecified. These choices materially determine the algorithmic model and cannot be verified from the record alone.

children.title: Normal–Tangential SQP Subproblems
children.top_down_role: SQP subproblems represented through normal and tangential step spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal–Tangential SQP Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained normal–tangential decomposition of an SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the linearized equality constraint \(c_k+A_kd=0\), decompose \(d=v+u\). Choose the normal step \(v\) to reduce \(\|c_k+A_kv\|\), and impose \(A_ku=0\) on the tangential step. The tangential quadratic model is
\[\min_u\;(g_k+B_kv)^{\mathsf T}u+\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}B_ku\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_ku=0,\quad\|v+u\|\leq\Delta_k.\]
Because \(A_ku=0\), adding \(u\) preserves the affine residual attained by \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal component reduces linearized infeasibility; a null-space tangential component improves the quadratic objective without changing that residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(d=v+u\) with \(A_ku=0\), \(c_k+A_kd=c_k+A_kv\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality-constrained normal-tangential identity and tangential quadratic model are mathematically consistent, and representation fits the leaf. A source is required for the selected decomposition, trust-region coupling, and the unspecified model used to choose the normal step.

children.title: Feasibility–Optimality Step Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural interactions between feasibility restoration and objective reduction within decomposed SQP steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Optimality Step Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite-step coupling for an equality-constrained SQP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the linearized constraint be \(Ad=-c\), and decompose the trial step as \(d=v+t\). The normal step \(v\) is chosen to reduce \(\lVert c+Av\rVert\), while the tangential step satisfies \(At=0\) and reduces the quadratic objective model. These tasks remain coupled through the shared globalization constraint, such as \(\lVert v+t\rVert\leq\Delta\), and through the linear term and curvature evaluated at \(v+t\). Consequently, independently optimal normal and tangential steps need not produce an admissible or model-optimal composite step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal step reduces linearized infeasibility and a null-space tangential step improves optimality, but their sum must jointly satisfy globalization and quadratic-model requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The composite step must enforce \(d=v+t\), \(At=0\), and \(\lVert v+t\rVert\leq\Delta\) jointly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained linear least squares with an arbitrary real residual matrix; rank deficiency is allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n} and y\in\mathbb{R}^m, and define f(x)=\tfrac12\lVert Jx-y\rVert_2^2. Then \nabla f(x)=J^T(Jx-y), \nabla^2 f(x)=J^TJ\succeq0, and f is convex. Moreover, x^* is a global minimizer if and only if J^TJx^*=J^Ty.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauss–Newton Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained Gauss–Newton model for nonlinear least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2\), with residual \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) differentiable at \(x\), the Gauss–Newton subproblem is \[\min_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert r(x)+J(x)d\rVert_2^2.\] Equivalently, after discarding the constant term, it minimizes \(\tfrac12 d^{\mathsf T}J^{\mathsf T}Jd+(J^{\mathsf T}r)^{\mathsf T}d\). Every minimizer satisfies \(J^{\mathsf T}Jd=-J^{\mathsf T}r\); it is unique when \(J\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearizing the residual produces a linear least-squares step whose quadratic Hessian is the Jacobian Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is differentiable at the current point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in\operatorname*{argmin}_u\lVert r+Ju\rVert_2^2\) and hence \(J^{\mathsf T}Jd=-J^{\mathsf T}r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Least-Squares Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tikhonov-regularized linearized least-squares model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(\lambda>0\), the regularized subproblem is \[\min_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Jd+r\rVert_2^2+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\lVert Ld\rVert_2^2.\] Its minimizers solve \((J^{\mathsf T}J+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}L)d=-J^{\mathsf T}r\). The objective is strictly convex, and the minimizer is unique, exactly when \(\ker J\cap\ker L=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization adds a weighted squared seminorm to least squares; uniqueness holds precisely when the data and regularization operators have no common null direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniqueness holds if and only if \(\ker J\cap\ker L=\{0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Linear Least-Squares Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear least squares over a polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For data \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\), \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^q\), a constrained linear least-squares subproblem is \[\min_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Jd+r\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ad=b,\quad Gd\leq h.\] It is the convex quadratic program with Hessian \(J^{\mathsf T}J\), linear coefficient \(J^{\mathsf T}r\), and feasible set \(K=\{d:Ad=b,\ Gd\leq h\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained linear least-squares problem minimizes a squared affine residual over linear equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem is a convex quadratic program because \(J^{\mathsf T}J\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality-Constrained Quadratic Program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a quadratic objective subject to linear equality constraints, without curvature or rank assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An equality-constrained quadratic program has the form
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12 x^T Gx+h^Tx+c
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+b=0,
\]
where \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times n}\) are constant matrices, and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}\) are constant data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained quadratic program minimizes one half x transpose G x plus h transpose x plus c, subject to the linear equality Ax plus b equals zero. No curvature assumption on G or rank assumption on A is imposed in this definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\frac12x^TGx+h^Tx+c:Ax+b=0\right\}\text{ is an equality-constrained quadratic program.}

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Rank Feasible Equality-QP Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posed equality QP with independent constraints and positive reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and suppose \(\operatorname{rank}A=m\). Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b.\] Let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\), then the equality QP has a unique primal minimizer and a unique equality multiplier. Equivalently, the KKT matrix \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\] is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent equalities and positive-definite curvature on their null space give a unique primal solution, a unique multiplier, and a nonsingular KKT system.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal minimizer and equality multiplier are unique, and \(\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the equality-constraint null space

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Equality-QP Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible equality QP with redundant equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b.\] Suppose \(b\in\operatorname{range}A\) and \(\operatorname{rank}A<m\). Then every nonzero \(w\in\ker A^{\mathsf T}\) gives a null vector \((0,w)\) of the unreduced KKT matrix, so that matrix is singular. If \((x_*,y_*)\) satisfies the KKT equations, then \((x_*,y_*+w)\) also satisfies them for every \(w\in\ker A^{\mathsf T}\). The primal minimizer is nevertheless unique if \(z^{\mathsf T}Hz>0\) for every nonzero \(z\in\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant equality rows make the unreduced KKT system singular and the multipliers nonunique, although positive curvature on the constraint null space still gives a unique primal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unreduced KKT matrix is singular and KKT multipliers are nonunique; the primal minimizer is unique if \(z^{\mathsf T}Hz>0\) for all nonzero \(z\in\ker A\).

notation.meaning: left-null vector of the equality matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Equality-Constraint Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic infeasibility certificate for equality-constrained QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). The system \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent if and only if \(b\notin\operatorname{range}A\), equivalently if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \[A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y\neq0.\] Thus such a vector \(y\) certifies that every quadratic program subject to \(Ax=b\) has an empty feasible set, independently of its objective coefficients.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\neq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced-Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary case where reduced quadratic curvature is positive semidefinite but singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Suppose \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ax_p=b\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Define \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) and \(q=Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\). If \(R\succeq0\) is singular, the equality QP has a minimizer if and only if \(q\in\operatorname{range}R\), equivalently \(q\perp\ker R\). In that case its reduced minimizers solve \(Rz=-q\), and its primal minimizers are nonunique. If \(q\notin\operatorname{range}R\), the objective is unbounded below on \(\{x:Ax=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With singular positive-semidefinite reduced curvature, a minimizer exists exactly when the reduced linear coefficient is orthogonal to every null-curvature direction; otherwise the feasible quadratic is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizer exists if and only if \(q\in\operatorname{range}R\); otherwise the equality QP is unbounded below.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the equality-constraint null space

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Reduced-Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded equality-QP regime caused by negative feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Suppose \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ax_p=b\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). If the reduced Hessian \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) has a negative eigenvalue, then there exists a nonzero feasible direction \(p\in\ker A\) with \(p^{\mathsf T}Hp<0\). The quadratic objective \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) is then unbounded below on \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\), so the equality QP has no finite global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative curvature in the equality-constraint null space makes the feasible quadratic objective unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality-constrained quadratic objective is unbounded below on \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Curvature Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral boundary separating strictly convex and indefinite reduced quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H(t)=H(t)^\top\) depend continuously on \(t\), let \(A\) be fixed, and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Define \(R(t)=Z^\top H(t)Z\). The reduced-curvature transition boundary is
\[\mathcal B=\{t:\lambda_{\min}(R(t))=0\}.\]
On \(\{t:\lambda_{\min}(R(t))>0\}\), the quadratic is strictly convex along every nonzero feasible direction. On \(\{t:\lambda_{\min}(R(t))<0\}\), a feasible negative-curvature direction exists. Thus a continuous transition between these regimes must meet \(\mathcal B\), where reduced curvature is positive semidefinite but singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transition occurs when the smallest reduced-Hessian eigenvalue reaches zero, separating positive-definite reduced curvature from a regime containing feasible negative curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B=\{t:\lambda_{\min}(Z^\top H(t)Z)=0\}\) separates the positive-definite and indefinite reduced-curvature regimes.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for feasible directions in the null space of the equality matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality certificate for a finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Hx+g^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(H=H^\top\), and let \(Z\) span \(\ker A\). A pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) certifies that \(x^*\) is a global minimizer when
\[Ax^*=b,\qquad Hx^*+g+A^\top\lambda^*=0,\qquad Z^\top HZ\succeq0.\]
Conversely, every global minimizer admits such a multiplier, and the reduced Hessian is positive semidefinite. The certificate is directly verifiable by primal and stationarity residuals together with a positive-semidefiniteness test on the feasible-direction subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility, KKT stationarity, and positive-semidefinite curvature on feasible directions jointly certify—and are necessary for—global equality-QP optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^\top\) and the affine set \(\{x:Ax=b\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) globally minimizes \(q\) over \(Ax=b\) if and only if the displayed certificate holds for some \(\lambda^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Optimality Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First- and second-order characterization expressed entirely in feasible null-space coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a feasible point \(x_p\) for \(Ax=b\), and let \(Z\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Every feasible point has the form \(x_p+Zy\), and
\[q(x_p+Zy)=q(x_p)+r^\top y+\tfrac12y^\top Ry,\qquad r=Z^\top(Hx_p+g),\quad R=Z^\top HZ.\]
The point \(x_p+Zy^*\) is a global minimizer exactly when \(Ry^*+r=0\) and \(R\succeq0\). It is the unique global minimizer exactly when \(Ry^*+r=0\) and \(R\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In null-space coordinates, global optimality is reduced stationarity plus a positive-semidefinite reduced Hessian; positive definiteness gives uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and spans \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global and unique optimality are characterized respectively by \(Ry^*+r=0\) with \(R\succeq0\), and by \(Ry^*+r=0\) with \(R\succ0\).

notation.meaning: Null-space coordinate of a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Global Equality-QP Solution under Positive Reduced Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-Hessian sufficient condition for uniqueness and global optimality in an equality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \frac12x^TGx+x^Tc\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b.\] Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\). If \(Z^TGZ\succ0\), then the primal component \(x^\star\) of the unique pair satisfying \[\begin{bmatrix}G&-A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x^\star\\\lambda^\star\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-c\\b\end{bmatrix}\] is the unique global solution of the equality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the equality constraints have full row rank and the Hessian is positive definite on their null space, then the primal component of the KKT solution is the unique global minimizer of the equality-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x^\star\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}\left(\frac12x^TGx+x^Tc\right).

children.title: Attained Equality-QP Minima
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which an equality-constrained quadratic objective attains a finite minimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Attained Equality-QP Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact attainment criterion for a feasible equality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Ax_p=b\), let \(Z\) have full column rank and span \(\ker A\), and define \(R=Z^\top HZ\) and \(r=Z^\top(Hx_p+g)\). For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Hx+g^\top x\), the minimum over \(Ax=b\) is attained if and only if
\[R\succeq0\quad\text{and}\quad r\in\operatorname{range}(R).\]
When these conditions hold, the complete minimizer set is
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}q(x)=\{x_p+Zy:Ry=-r\}.\]
Equivalently, any particular solution \(y_0\) gives the affine set \(x_p+Zy_0+Z\ker R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-QP attains its minimum exactly when its reduced Hessian is positive semidefinite and its reduced linear term lies in the reduced Hessian’s range.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Attainment is equivalent to \(R\succeq0\) and \(r\in\operatorname{range}(R)\), with minimizers satisfying \(Ry=-r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Equality-QP Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-curvature criterion for existence of exactly one feasible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the affine set \(\{x:Ax=b\}\) be nonempty, let \(Z\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and set \(R=Z^\top HZ\). The equality-constrained quadratic \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Hx+g^\top x\) has a unique global minimizer if and only if
\[R\succ0.\]
In that case, for any feasible \(x_p\), the unique reduced coordinate and minimizer are
\[y^*=-R^{-1}Z^\top(Hx_p+g),\qquad x^*=x_p+Zy^*.\]
Positive definiteness is understood vacuously when \(\ker A=\{0\}\), in which case the feasible set is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible equality-QP has exactly one minimizer precisely when the Hessian is positive definite on all nonzero feasible directions.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and spans \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimizer is unique if and only if \(Z^\top HZ\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Equality-QP Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion and affine representation for a non-singleton minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x_p\) satisfying \(Ax_p=b\), let \(Z\) have full column rank and span \(\ker A\), and define \(R=Z^\top HZ\) and \(r=Z^\top(Hx_p+g)\). The equality-constrained quadratic has multiple global minimizers if and only if
\[R\succeq0,\qquad r\in\operatorname{range}(R),\qquad \ker R\neq\{0\}.\]
If \(Ry_0=-r\), its complete minimizer set is
\[\{x_p+Z(y_0+v):v\in\ker R\}.\]
Distinct null vectors give distinct minimizers because \(Z\) has full column rank, and the objective is constant along these reduced null directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple minimizers occur exactly when the reduced problem is solvable and convex but its reduced Hessian has a nontrivial null space.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiple minimizers exist exactly when \(R\succeq0\), \(r\in\operatorname{range}(R)\), and \(\ker R\neq\{0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Existing Equality-QP Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability criterion for multipliers associated with a fixed feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-QP with Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda)=\tfrac12x^\top Hx+g^\top x+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)\), fix a feasible point \(x\). Its multiplier set is
\[\Lambda(x)=\{\lambda:Hx+g+A^\top\lambda=0\}.\]
This set is nonempty if and only if
\[-(Hx+g)\in\operatorname{range}(A^\top),\]
equivalently, \(Z^\top(Hx+g)=0\) for any matrix \(Z\) spanning \(\ker A\). Whenever \(x\) is a local minimizer over the nonempty affine feasible set, this orthogonality condition holds, so at least one equality multiplier exists even when \(A\) is row-rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point has an equality multiplier exactly when its negative objective gradient lies in the range of the transposed constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda(x)\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(-(Hx+g)\in\operatorname{range}(A^\top)\), equivalently \(Z^\top(Hx+g)=0\).

notation.meaning: Multiplier set associated with the feasible point \(x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Equality-QP Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank criterion for uniqueness of an existing equality multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a feasible point \(x\) for which \(\Lambda(x)=\{\lambda:Hx+g+A^\top\lambda=0\}\) is nonempty. If \(\lambda_0\in\Lambda(x)\), then
\[\Lambda(x)=\lambda_0+\ker(A^\top).\]
Consequently, the equality multiplier associated with \(x\) is unique if and only if
\[\ker(A^\top)=\{0\},\]
equivalently, \(A\) has full row rank. This criterion concerns multiplier uniqueness at a fixed primal point; it is independent of whether the primal minimizer itself is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a multiplier exists, it is unique exactly when the equality matrix has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\Lambda(x)|=1\) if and only if \(\ker(A^\top)=\{0\}\), equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(A)\) equals the number of rows of \(A\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Equality-QP Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine characterization of multiplier ambiguity caused by redundant equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a feasible point \(x\), and suppose a multiplier \(\lambda_0\) satisfies \(Hx+g+A^\top\lambda_0=0\). The complete multiplier set is
\[\Lambda(x)=\lambda_0+\ker(A^\top).\]
Hence multipliers are nonunique if and only if
\[\ker(A^\top)\neq\{0\},\]
equivalently, \(A\) is not of full row rank. Every nonzero \(w\in\ker(A^\top)\) generates the distinct multipliers \(\lambda_0+tw\) for \(t\in\mathbb R\), all producing the same stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a multiplier exists, redundant equality rows make it nonunique; all multipliers form an affine translate of the null space of the transposed constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multipliers are nonunique if and only if \(\ker(A^\top)\neq\{0\}\), and \(\Lambda(x)=\lambda_0+\ker(A^\top)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Nonexistence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stationarity representability at a feasible but nonoptimal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible point \(x\), no equality multiplier satisfies the KKT stationarity equation precisely when
\[-(Hx+g)\notin\operatorname{range}(A^\top).\]
Equivalently, for any \(Z\) spanning \(\ker A\),
\[Z^\top(Hx+g)\neq0.\]
In this regime the objective has a nonzero first derivative along some feasible direction, so \(x\) cannot be a local minimizer over the affine feasible set. Thus multiplier nonexistence can occur for arbitrary feasible trial points, but not for an attained local or global equality-QP minimizer in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier does not exist when the objective gradient has a nonzero feasible-direction component; such a feasible point cannot be locally optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda(x)=\varnothing\) if and only if \(-(Hx+g)\notin\operatorname{range}(A^\top)\), equivalently \(Z^\top(Hx+g)\neq0\).

notation.meaning: Set of multipliers satisfying stationarity at \(x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite KKT Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct full-space solve using a symmetric pivoted indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(H=H^\top\), \(A\), \(g\), and \(b\), form
\[K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^\top\\A&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad d=\begin{pmatrix}-g\\b\end{pmatrix}.\]
Compute a stable symmetric-pivoted factorization \(P^\top KP=LDL^\top\), where \(D\) has permitted \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks. Solve successively
\[Lw=P^\top d,\qquad Dz=w,\qquad L^\top u=z,\qquad \begin{pmatrix}x\\\lambda\end{pmatrix}=Pu.\]
Stop successfully and return \((x,\lambda)\) when the primal and stationarity residuals meet prescribed tolerances. Report singularity or invoke regularization when an acceptable factorization or residual cannot be obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the symmetric KKT equations by a pivoted block LDL-transpose factorization, then accept the primal-dual pair only after residual checks.
assumptions_latex: The KKT system is consistent and nonsingular for an unregularized unique solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned pair approximately satisfies \(Hx+g+A^\top\lambda=0\) and \(Ax=b\) to the prescribed tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent augmented KKT formulation for an equality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the quadratic program \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^THx+g^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), choose \(\rho\ge0\) and solve
\[\begin{bmatrix}H+\rho A^TA&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g+\rho A^Tb\\b\end{bmatrix}.\]
Output \((x,\lambda)\) when the primal and stationarity residuals meet the prescribed linear-solve tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a weighted constraint Gramian to the primal KKT block, solve the augmented saddle-point system, and return the corresponding exact KKT solution when the residual tolerances are met.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(A\) has full row rank and \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Hx+g+A^T\lambda=0\) and \(Ax=b\) for an exact solve.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Full-Space Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual diagonal regularization of a full-space KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given regularization parameters \(\delta>0\) and \(\gamma>0\), solve
\[\begin{bmatrix}H+\delta I&A^T\\A&-\gamma I\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x_{\delta,\gamma}\\\lambda_{\delta,\gamma}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\b\end{bmatrix}.\]
Thus the output satisfies \(Hx_{\delta,\gamma}+g+A^T\lambda_{\delta,\gamma}=-\delta x_{\delta,\gamma}\) and \(Ax_{\delta,\gamma}-b=\gamma\lambda_{\delta,\gamma}\). Reduce \(\delta\) and \(\gamma\) until these residual bounds and the linear-solve tolerance meet the requested accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularize both diagonal KKT blocks, solve the resulting nonsingular full-space system, and decrease regularization until the original KKT residuals are acceptable.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(g,b\) have compatible dimensions.
The displayed regularized matrix is nonsingular for the selected \(\delta,\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Hx_{\delta,\gamma}+g+A^T\lambda_{\delta,\gamma}\|=\delta\|x_{\delta,\gamma}\|\) and \(\|Ax_{\delta,\gamma}-b\|=\gamma\|\lambda_{\delta,\gamma}\|\).

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Null-Space Basis Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction using an orthonormal basis obtained from a complete orthogonal factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), compute
\[A^T=[Y\ Z]\begin{bmatrix}R\\0\end{bmatrix},\]
where \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\), \([Y\ Z]\) is orthogonal, and \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Solve \(R^Tp=b\), set \(x_p=Yp\), solve
\[(Z^THZ)z=-Z^T(Hx_p+g),\]
and output \(x=x_p+Zz\). If a multiplier is required, solve \(R\lambda=-Y^T(Hx+g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the constraint transpose orthogonally, construct a feasible particular point, solve the quadratic problem in orthonormal null-space coordinates, and optionally recover the multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(m\le n\), and \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\), \(Hx+g+A^T\lambda=0\), and \(x\) is the unique minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental Null-Space Basis Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse algebraic null-space reduction based on a nonsingular constraint submatrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), permute the columns of \(A\) and write \(A=[B\ N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Form
\[Z=\begin{bmatrix}-B^{-1}N\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix},\qquad x_p=\begin{bmatrix}B^{-1}b\\0\end{bmatrix}.\]
Solve
\[(Z^THZ)z=-Z^T(Hx_p+g)\]
and output \(x=x_p+Zz\). Implement products involving \(B^{-1}\) by solves with \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose dependent variables through a nonsingular constraint block, construct a fundamental null-space basis and feasible point, and solve the reduced quadratic system.
assumptions_latex: \(m\le n\), and \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=x_p+Zz\) is feasible and uniquely minimizes the equality-constrained quadratic objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Null-Space Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free null-space reduction through an orthogonal projector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define
\[P=I_n-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A.\]
Apply \(P\) through solves with \(AA^T\). Choose \(x_p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ax_p=b\), and solve for \(w\in\operatorname{range}(P)\)
\[PHPw=-P(Hx_p+g),\qquad w=Pw.\]
A projected Krylov implementation uses products \(v\mapsto P(H(Pv))\). Output \(x=x_p+w\) without constructing a null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply an implicit orthogonal null-space projector and solve the projected optimality equation without explicitly constructing null-space coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) and \(P(Hx+g)=0\), equivalently \(Hx+g\in\operatorname{range}(A^T)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orthogonal Null-Space Projector and Basis-Free Application
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the identity-metric case and distinguishes the explicit basis formula from the possibility of applying the projector without explicitly representing the basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the columns of $Z$ form a basis for $\ker A$. When $H=I$, the projected-CG operator is the orthogonal projector onto $\ker A$,
\[
P_I=Z(Z^TZ)^{-1}Z^T.
\]
Although this formula uses $Z$, the product $P_Ir$ can be computed without an explicit representation of the null-space basis $Z$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When H is the identity and the columns of Z form a basis for the null space of A, Z times the inverse of Z transpose Z times Z transpose is the orthogonal projector onto that null space. The projector can be applied to a residual without explicitly representing Z.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_I=Z(Z^TZ)^{-1}Z^T\text{ is the orthogonal projector onto }\ker A,\qquad P_Ir\text{ can be evaluated without explicitly representing }Z.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Solution Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution of an equality-constrained quadratic program through its reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\), and let \(x_p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(Ax_p=b\). Form
\[H_r=Z^THZ,\qquad g_r=Z^T(Hx_p+g).\]
Solve \(H_rz=-g_r\), output \(x=x_p+Zz\), and recover \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) from \(A^T\lambda=-(Hx+g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent feasible points in null-space coordinates, solve the reduced-Hessian equation, and recover the equality multiplier from stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=x_p-ZH_r^{-1}g_r\) is the unique primal solution and satisfies the KKT equations with a unique \(\lambda\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Block-Elimination Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of dependent primal variables before solving a smaller quadratic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), partition \(x=(x_B,x_N)\) and \(A=[B\ N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Enforce feasibility using
\[x_B=B^{-1}(b-Nx_N).\]
Substitute this expression into \(\tfrac12x^THx+g^Tx\). The resulting quadratic in \(x_N\) has Hessian \(Z^THZ\), where
\[Z=\begin{bmatrix}-B^{-1}N\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}.\]
Solve its stationarity equation, reconstruct \(x_B\), and recover \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) from \(B^T\lambda=-(Hx+g)_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the equality constraints to eliminate dependent primal variables, solve the remaining unconstrained quadratic, and reconstruct the multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(m\le n\), \(A\) has full row rank, and the selected block \(B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reconstructed \((x,\lambda)\) satisfies \(Hx+g+A^T\lambda=0\) and \(Ax=b\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Schur-Complement Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range-space elimination through the multiplier Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), consider the KKT equations \(Hx+g+A^T\lambda=0\) and \(Ax=b\). Form or apply
\[S=AH^{-1}A^T,\]
solve
\[S\lambda=-b-AH^{-1}g,\]
and recover
\[x=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda).\]
Implement each application of \(H^{-1}\) by a linear solve, and stop when the primal and stationarity residuals satisfy their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal vector, solve the constraint-sized multiplier Schur-complement system, and recover the primal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\succ0\), and the recovered \((x,\lambda)\) uniquely satisfies the KKT equations for an exact solve.

children.title: Null-Space-Dominant Hybrid Methods
children.top_down_role: Hybrid equality-QP solvers whose principal reduced computation occurs in the null space.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space-Dominant Hybrid Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid elimination retaining a null-space reduced solve as its principal operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a feasible point \(x_p\) and a null-space operator \(Z\) with \(AZ=0\). Solve the principal reduced equation \((Z^THZ)z=-Z^T(Hx_p+g)\), set \(x=x_p+Zz\), and compute \(\lambda\) by a range-space least-squares solve \(\min_y\|A^Ty+(Hx+g)\|_2\). If the feasibility residual exceeds tolerance, apply the range correction \(x\leftarrow x+A^T(AA^T)^{-1}(b-Ax)\), then repeat the reduced correction. Output when both KKT residuals pass tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a null-space solve for the main step and range-space solves only to restore feasibility or recover multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At exact termination, \(Ax=b\) and \(Hx+g+A^T\lambda=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source identifies this particular null-space-dominant hybrid, its feasibility-correction loop, or its stopping policy. The construction is plausible but cannot be treated as an established algorithm without supporting evidence.

children.title: Range-Space-Dominant Hybrid Methods
children.top_down_role: Hybrid equality-QP solvers whose principal reduced computation occurs in the constraint range space.

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space-Dominant Hybrid Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid elimination retaining a multiplier range-space solve as its principal operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the multiplier Schur equation \(AH^{-1}A^T\lambda=-b-AH^{-1}g\) as the principal solve and recover \(x=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda)\). If applications of \(H^{-1}\) are inexact, compute the dual residual \(r_d=Hx+g+A^T\lambda\), project the correction into \(\ker A\), and solve \((Z^THZ)z=-Z^Tr_d\). Update \(x\leftarrow x+Zz\) and repeat until primal and dual residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a multiplier Schur-complement solve for the main step and null-space corrections to remove remaining dual residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At exact termination, the output satisfies \(Ax=b\) and \(Hx+g+A^T\lambda=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed hybrid. Moreover, inexact applications of H inverse can leave a primal residual, while the stated null-space correction preserves that residual and supplies no feasibility correction.

children.title: Adaptive Space-Switching Methods
children.top_down_role: Hybrid solvers that select or change reduced spaces according to problem structure or numerical behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Space-Switching Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-driven switching between null-space and range-space equality-QP formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), compute primal and dual residuals \(r_p^k=Ax_k-b\) and \(r_d^k=Hx_k+g+A^T\lambda_k\). If \(\|r_p^k\|_2>\tau\|r_d^k\|_2\), take a range-space feasibility correction using \(AA^T\); otherwise take a null-space stationarity correction using \(Z^THZ\). Accept a correction only if the combined residual norm decreases; otherwise switch spaces. Stop when \(\max\{\|r_p^k\|_2,\|r_d^k\|_2\}\le\varepsilon\), and output \((x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare primal and dual residuals, choose the correction space predicted to address the larger error, and switch when progress fails.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank and \(H=H^T\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination certifies \(\max\{\|Ax_k-b\|_2,\|Hx_k+g+A^T\lambda_k\|_2\}\le\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual threshold and switch-on-failure policy appear to be an uncited candidate design. The range-space and null-space corrections are not specified sufficiently to establish a reproducible algorithm or convergence behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate Gradient on Reduced Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic conjugate gradient applied to a positive-definite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\), and \(x_p\in\mathbb R^n\). Form
\[H_r=Z^THZ,\qquad c=-Z^T(Hx_p+g).\]
Choose \(z_0\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\), set \(r_0=c-H_rz_0\) and \(p_0=r_0\). At iteration \(k\), stop and output \(x=x_p+Zz_k\) if \(\|r_k\|_2\le\varepsilon\). Otherwise set
\[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{p_k^TH_rp_k},\qquad z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kp_k,\qquad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kH_rp_k.\]
If \(\|r_{k+1}\|_2\le\varepsilon\), output \(x=x_p+Zz_{k+1}\). Otherwise set
\[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\qquad p_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kp_k,\]
and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run conjugate gradient on the positive-definite reduced Hessian, checking convergence before each division, and map the reduced iterate to a feasible primal vector.
assumptions_latex: \(AZ=0\), \(Ax_p=b\), and the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In exact arithmetic, CG reaches the reduced solution in at most \(n-m\) iterations, and every reconstructed iterate \(x_k=x_p+Zz_k\) is feasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-Space Reduction of an Equality-Constrained Quadratic Program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction and reconstruction equations underlying CG on an equality-QP reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\). Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker A\), and choose \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) so that \(AY\) is nonsingular. With \(x^*=Yx_Y+Zx_z\), feasibility determines \(x_Y\) from \(AYx_Y=b\). The remaining coordinates minimize \[\frac12x_z^T(Z^TGZ)x_z+x_z^Tc_z,\qquad c_z=Z^TGYx_Y+Z^Tc,\] and satisfy \[(Z^TGZ)x_z=-c_z.\] If \(Z^TGZ\succ0\), the reduced system has a unique solution and can be solved by CG; a supplied SPD matrix \(W_{zz}\) may be used for preconditioned CG. Substitution into \(x^*=Yx_Y+Zx_z\) reconstructs the QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space decomposition separates a particular feasible component from free tangent-space coordinates. The latter solve an unconstrained quadratic problem whose Hessian is Z-transpose G Z. When that reduced Hessian is positive definite, CG or preconditioned CG can solve the unique reduced system, and the original QP solution is reconstructed from both components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (Z^TGZ)x_z=-\left(Z^TGYx_Y+Z^Tc\right),\qquad x^*=Yx_Y+Zx_z.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned CG Recurrence for a Reduced Equality-QP System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extracted iteration for preconditioned CG applied to \((Z^TGZ)x_z=-c_z\); it makes no standalone convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_z=Z^TGZ\succ0\) and \(W_{zz}=W_{zz}^T\succ0\). Choose \(x_z\), and initialize \[r_z=K_zx_z+c_z,\qquad g_z=W_{zz}^{-1}r_z,\qquad d_z=-g_z.\] Until a termination test is satisfied, compute \[\alpha=\frac{r_z^Tg_z}{d_z^TK_zd_z},\qquad x_z\leftarrow x_z+\alpha d_z,\qquad r_z^+\leftarrow r_z+\alpha K_zd_z,\] \[g_z^+\leftarrow W_{zz}^{-1}r_z^+,\qquad \beta=\frac{(r_z^+)^Tg_z^+}{r_z^Tg_z},\qquad d_z\leftarrow-g_z^++\beta d_z,\] followed by \((g_z,r_z)\leftarrow(g_z^+,r_z^+)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize the reduced-system residual, apply the inverse preconditioner, and use the negative preconditioned residual as the first direction. Each iteration computes the PCG step length, updates the point and residual, reapplies the preconditioner, computes the new direction coefficient, and continues until a termination test holds.
assumptions_latex: \text{The iteration has not already terminated when the displayed quotients are evaluated.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed recurrence applies preconditioned CG to }K_zx_z=-c_z\text{ until the prescribed termination test is satisfied.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stopping, Matrix-Free Evaluation, and Preconditioning for Reduced-System CG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optional stopping criterion, matrix-free implementation conditions, and admissible preconditioners for reduced-system CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For reduced-system CG with \(K_z=Z^TGZ\succ0\) and \(W_{zz}=W_{zz}^T\succ0\), one possible stopping test is that \(r_z^TW_{zz}^{-1}r_z\) be sufficiently small. Explicit formation of \(K_z\) is unnecessary when its matrix-vector products can be computed; explicit formation of \(Z\) is likewise unnecessary when products by \(Z\) and \(Z^T\) are available. The preconditioner may be chosen to cluster the eigenvalues and reduce the spectral spread of \(W_{zz}^{-1/2}K_zW_{zz}^{-1/2}\). The ideal choice \(W_{zz}=K_z\) makes this matrix equal to \(I\). An admissible structured family is \[W_{zz}=Z^THZ,\] where \(H=H^T\) and \(Z^THZ\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-system CG may stop when the preconditioned residual norm is sufficiently small. It can be implemented through matrix-vector products without forming the reduced Hessian, and the basis itself need not be formed if products with it and its transpose are available. An SPD preconditioner may be selected to cluster the scaled spectrum; the reduced Hessian is ideal, while Z-transpose H Z gives a structured family when it is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_z^TW_{zz}^{-1}r_z\ \text{small may be used as a stopping test},\qquad W_{zz}=Z^THZ\succ0,\qquad W_{zz}=K_z\Rightarrow W_{zz}^{-1/2}K_zW_{zz}^{-1/2}=I.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Conjugate-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space projected CG for a strictly convex equality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given feasible \(x_0\), set \(r_0=-P(Hx_0+c)\) and \(p_0=r_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), while \(\|r_k\|_2>\varepsilon\), compute \(\alpha_k=(r_k^\top r_k)/(p_k^\top Hp_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and \(r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kPHp_k\). Set \(\beta_k=(r_{k+1}^\top r_{k+1})/(r_k^\top r_k)\) and \(p_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kp_k\). Return the first \(x_k\) satisfying \(\|r_k\|_2\leq\varepsilon\). Every iterate satisfies \(Ax_k=b\), and in exact arithmetic termination occurs after at most \(\dim(\ker A)\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected CG preserves equality feasibility and, for a positive-definite reduced Hessian, reaches the restricted quadratic minimizer in at most the null-space dimension in exact arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ax_0=b\).
\(H=H^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|P(Hx_k+c)\|_2\leq\varepsilon\) at termination, and exact arithmetic terminates in at most \(\dim(\ker A)\) iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Preconditioned Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint preconditioning implemented through saddle-point solves that return null-space directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(r_0=-Pg(x_0)\), obtain \((z_0,y_0)\) from \(Mz_0+A^\top y_0=r_0\) and \(Az_0=0\), and set \(p_0=z_0\). At iteration \(k\), use \(\alpha_k=(r_k^\top z_k)/(p_k^\top Hp_k)\), update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) and \(r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kPHp_k\), and solve the constrained preconditioner system for \(z_{k+1}\). Set \(\beta_k=(r_{k+1}^\top z_{k+1})/(r_k^\top z_k)\) and \(p_{k+1}=z_{k+1}+\beta_kp_k\). Stop when \(\|r_k\|_2\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each preconditioner application solves a saddle-point system that produces a null-space direction for preconditioned conjugate gradients while preserving equality feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ax_0=b\).
\(H=H^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(M=M^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) are positive definite on \(\ker A\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax_k=b\) for every iterate, and the iteration is preconditioned CG on the reduced Hessian without an explicit null-space basis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-face reduction principle for inequality-constrained QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Motivating principle for feasible active-set methods; it is not stated as a formal equivalence without the accompanying optimality lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linearly constrained quadratic program, inequalities inactive at a solution impose no local equality restriction, whereas each active inequality satisfies \(a_i^T x^*=b_i\) and may be included as an equality in the solution face. Active-set methods therefore solve equality-constrained QP models associated with selected active faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a QP solution, inactive inequalities can be omitted from the face model, while active inequalities can be imposed as equalities. This motivates solving equality-constrained QP subproblems on candidate active sets.
assumptions_latex: a_i^T x=b_i\ \text{for }i\in E,\qquad a_i^T x\ge b_i\ \text{for }i\in I
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The local face model retains }E\cup I(x^*)\text{ as equalities and omits inactive inequalities.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility and descent invariants of the QP active-set algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the independently stated invariants and conditional finite-termination conclusion. The unfinished nontermination argument in the extract is excluded rather than promoted into a theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iterates generated by the feasible active-set QP algorithm,
\[x_k\in X,\qquad Q(x_{k+1})\le Q(x_k)\quad\text{for every }k.\]
Whenever \(d_k\ne0\) and \(\alpha_k>0\),
\[Q(x_{k+1})<Q(x_k).\]
If the algorithm terminates after finitely many iterations, its terminal point is a KKT point of the original QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every iterate remains feasible and the objective never increases. A nonzero direction taken with positive step length gives strict decrease. If the algorithm terminates finitely, the returned point satisfies the original QP KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is defined by finitely many affine equality and inequality constraints}
\text{the working-set subproblems are solved as prescribed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in X,\quad Q(x_{k+1})\le Q(x_k)\ \forall k;\qquad d_k\ne0,\ \alpha_k>0\Rightarrow Q(x_{k+1})<Q(x_k);\qquad \text{finite termination}\Rightarrow\text{KKT termination.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-minimizer and KKT correspondence on the active QP face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates a mixed affine-constrained QP to the equality-constrained QP determined by the active inequalities at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=g^Tx+\tfrac12x^TGx\), \(X=\{x:a_i^Tx=b_i\ (i\in E),\ a_i^Tx\ge b_i\ (i\in I)\}\), and \(I(x^*)=\{i\in I:a_i^Tx^*=b_i\}\). If \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of \(q\) on \(X\), then \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of \(q\) subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for every \(i\in E\cup I(x^*)\). Conversely, if \(x^*\in X\) is a KKT point of this equality-constrained face problem and its multipliers satisfy \(\lambda_i^*\ge0\) for all \(i\in I(x^*)\), then \(x^*\) is a KKT point of the original mixed-constraint QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimizer of the original QP remains a local minimizer when all inequalities active there are imposed as equalities. Conversely, a feasible KKT point of that active-face equality problem is a KKT point of the original QP when every active-inequality multiplier is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local-minimal on }X\Rightarrow x^*\text{ local-minimal on the active face};\quad [x^*\in X,\ x^*\text{ face-KKT},\ \lambda_i^*\ge0\ \forall i\in I(x^*)]\Rightarrow x^*\text{ is KKT for }X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible working-set iteration for convex linearly constrained QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One iteration of the primal feasible active-set method, including an equality-constrained face step, multiplier-based release, and first-blocking-constraint insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a feasible \(x_k\) and a working set satisfying \(E\subseteq S_k\subseteq E\cup I(x_k)\), solve
\[\min_d\ \tfrac12d^TGd+(Gx_k+g)^Td\quad\text{s.t.}\quad a_i^Td=0\quad(i\in S_k).\]
If \(d_k=0\) and \(\lambda_i^{(k)}\ge0\) for all \(i\in S_k\cap I\), terminate at a KKT point. If \(d_k=0\) and some such multiplier is negative, remove an index attaining the minimum negative multiplier. If \(d_k\ne0\), choose the largest feasible \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\):
\[\alpha_k=\min\left\{1,\min_{\substack{i\notin S_k\\a_i^Td_k<0}}\frac{b_i-a_i^Tx_k}{a_i^Td_k}\right\},\]
where the inner minimum is omitted when no blocking inequality exists, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). If \(\alpha_k<1\), add an inequality attaining the blocking ratio; otherwise retain the working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the equality-constrained QP on the current feasible face. A zero step with nonnegative working-set inequality multipliers gives KKT termination; a negative multiplier causes release of a most-negative constraint. For a nonzero step, move to the full trial point or the first blocking inequality and add that blocker, thereby preserving feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}\text{ remains feasible, and }S_k\text{ is updated by multiplier-based release or first-blocking-constraint insertion.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal feasible active-set algorithm for convex affine-constrained QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete stepwise algorithm using equality-constrained face solves, most-negative-multiplier deletion, and blocking-constraint insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a feasible \(x_1\) and set \(S_1=E\cup I(x_1)\). At iteration \(k\), solve the working-set equality-constrained QP for \(d_k\). If \(d_k=0\), compute multipliers from
\[Gx_k+g=\sum_{i\in S_k}\lambda_i^{(k)}a_i.\]
Terminate if \(\lambda_i^{(k)}\ge0\) for every \(i\in S_k\cap I\). Otherwise choose
\[i_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\substack{i\in S_k\cap I\\\lambda_i^{(k)}<0}}\lambda_i^{(k)},\]
remove \(i_k\), and keep \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). If \(d_k\ne0\), choose the largest feasible \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and, when \(\alpha_k<1\), add a blocking index \(j\notin S_k\) satisfying \(a_j^Tx_{k+1}=b_j\). Carry the resulting set forward as \(S_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a feasible point with all currently active constraints in the working set. Solve the equality-constrained QP on that set. At a zero step, stop when all working inequality multipliers are nonnegative; otherwise remove a most-negative-multiplier inequality. At a nonzero step, move as far as feasibility permits and add a first blocking inequality when the full step cannot be taken.
assumptions_latex: \text{each working-set equality-constrained subproblem has a computed solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The method either terminates after satisfying the multiplier sign test or produces a feasible next iterate and an updated working set.}

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-QP KKT Certificate Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for a convex quadratic program with affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}q(x)\) subject to \(Gx\leq h\), a pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT certificate when \(Gx^*\leq h\), \(\lambda^*\geq0\), \(Hx^*+c+G^\top\lambda^*=0\), and \(\lambda_i^*(G_ix^*-h_i)=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\). These conditions are directly checkable. A feasible point \(x^*\) is globally optimal if and only if it admits such a multiplier \(\lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic program with affine inequalities, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementary slackness form a necessary and sufficient global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is globally optimal if and only if it admits a KKT certificate \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb{R}^p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Curvature Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-cone curvature tests for a quadratic objective over affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a KKT pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\), define \(C(x^*,\lambda^*)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:G_id=0\text{ for }i\in I(x^*)\text{ with }\lambda_i^*>0,\ G_id\leq0\text{ for }i\in I(x^*)\text{ with }\lambda_i^*=0\}\). At a local minimizer satisfying KKT, \(d^\top Hd\geq0\) for every \(d\in C(x^*,\lambda^*)\). Conversely, KKT together with \(d^\top Hd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in C(x^*,\lambda^*)\) yields quadratic growth and strict local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order curvature is tested on feasible first-order directions not excluded by positive KKT multipliers; nonnegativity is necessary, while strict positivity on every nonzero critical direction is sufficient for strict local optimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\tfrac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Gx\leq h\), where \(H=H^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Second-order necessity requires \(d^\top Hd\geq0\) on the critical cone; strict positivity for every nonzero critical direction implies quadratic growth and strict local optimality.

children.title: Constraint Degeneracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Inequality-QP settings with deficient active-constraint geometry or nonregular local faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Degeneracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-dependence degeneracy of active affine constraints at a KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The active constraints are degenerate at \(x^*\) when their normals are linearly dependent, equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(G_{I(x^*)})<|I(x^*)|\). In this regime there is a nonzero \(v\in\mathbb{R}^{|I(x^*)|}\) such that \(G_{I(x^*)}^\top v=0\). Whenever both \(\lambda_{I(x^*)}^*\) and \(\lambda_{I(x^*)}^*+tv\) are nonnegative, they give the same stationarity equation. Degeneracy therefore permits, but does not require, nonunique KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active constraint normals are degenerate when they are linearly dependent; this creates null multiplier directions and can, but need not, make KKT multipliers nonunique.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \((x^*,\lambda^*)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\) satisfies the KKT conditions for an inequality QP with constraints \(Gx\leq h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constraint degeneracy is characterized by \(\operatorname{rank}(G_{I(x^*)})<|I(x^*)|\), and it permits nonunique active multipliers.
