children.title: Multifrontal KKT Solves
children.top_down_role: Sparse KKT factorization organized through multiple fronts linked by an elimination tree.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is sparse, symmetric, and has an elimination tree induced by a fixed ordering.
Every selected pivot block is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root-to-leaf factors define a direct solution of \(Kx=b\).

notation.meaning: dense frontal matrix associated with tree node v
update matrix contributed by node v to its parent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multifrontal direct solution with dense fronts organized by an elimination tree.

source_refs.locator: 4.3.5 Frontal and Multifrontal Methods p. 66

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Kx=b\) and elimination tree \(T\), visit its nodes in postorder. For each node \(v\), assemble \(F_v\) from the original entries assigned to \(v\) and the update matrices \(U_c\) of all children \(c\). Factor the fully summed variables in \(F_v\), and pass the resulting Schur complement \(U_v\) to the parent. At the root, complete the factorization. Perform the corresponding tree-ordered forward and backward substitutions and output \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifrontal solver assembles many dense fronts along an elimination tree, combines child updates, eliminates local variables, and solves with the resulting factors.

children.title: Assembly-Tree Parallelism
children.top_down_role: Concurrency and data movement exposed by multifrontal assembly-tree structure.

assumptions_latex: The multifrontal dependency structure is a rooted tree \(T\).
Each front reads only its assigned original entries and the completed update matrices of its children.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any schedule in which each parent starts after all its children finish is dependency-correct, and fronts in incomparable subtrees may execute concurrently.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Task parallelism exposed by a fixed multifrontal assembly tree.

source_refs.locator: 4.3.5 Frontal and Multifrontal Methods p. 66

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every node \(v\) of \(T\), assembly and elimination of its front may begin after every child contribution is complete, that is, when \(\tau_c\leq s_v\) for all \(c\in\operatorname{ch}(v)\). Consequently, fronts in distinct subtrees having no ancestor relation have no assembly dependency and may be processed concurrently. A schedule respects the assembly-tree dependencies exactly when \(\tau_c\leq s_v\) for every tree edge from a child \(c\) to its parent \(v\). Tree-level parallelism is generally greatest among incomparable fronts, while sufficiently large individual fronts may expose additional dense linear-algebra parallelism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent assembly-tree subtrees can be processed concurrently, while every parent front must start only after all child update matrices have been completed.
knowledge_statements.title: Assembly-Tree Parallelism

children.title: KKT Factorization Updates
children.top_down_role: Reuse of an existing factorization after additions or structured changes to a QP system.

assumptions_latex: An existing nonsingular symmetric factorization of \(K\) is available.
The modified matrix is \(\widehat K=K+UWU^{\top}\), where \(W\) is symmetric and has small order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The old factorization can be modified through a low-rank correction when the small correction system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic low-rank modification of a nonsingular symmetric KKT factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given factors of \(K\), solve \(KY=U\) and form the small matrix \(M=W^{-1}+U^{\top}Y\) when \(W\) is invertible. If \(M\) is nonsingular, then for each right-hand side \(b\), compute \(z=K^{-1}b\) using the stored factors and return \(x=z-YM^{-1}U^{\top}z\), which satisfies \(\widehat Kx=b\). A factor-update implementation may equivalently transform the stored symmetric factors directly, while preserving the same modified matrix and pivoting safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank KKT change can reuse the old factors by solving with the original matrix and factoring only a small correction system.

If \(M_-\) is singular or numerically unacceptable, reject the downdate and refactor \(\widetilde K\) with fresh pivot selection.

children.title: Update Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditioning, pivot, or inertia changes that make factor reuse unreliable.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Singularity or severe ill-conditioning of the small correction matrix marks the boundary where factor modification must be abandoned.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(M_\sigma=W^{-1}+\sigma U^{\top}K^{-1}U\). The determinant identity \(\det(K_\sigma)=\det(K)\det(W)\det(M_\sigma)\) up to the nonzero sign-dependent scalar factor implies that \(K_\sigma\) is singular exactly when \(M_\sigma\) is singular. Even before singularity, large \(\kappa(M_\sigma)\), unacceptable pivot growth, or loss of the required inertia makes the modified factors unreliable; the modification should then be rejected in favor of a newly pivoted factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correction matrix becoming singular is the exact algebraic failure boundary; poor conditioning, pivot growth, or wrong inertia supplies earlier numerical rejection criteria.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-Hessian inertia formula for a KKT matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates the inertia of a full-row-rank equality-constrained KKT matrix to the inertia of its reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\in\mathbb{S}^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), and define \[K=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Then \[\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(Z^TGZ)+(m,m,0),\] where inertia triples are added componentwise. Consequently, if \(Z^TGZ\succ0\), then \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-row-rank equality-constraint matrix, the KKT matrix has the inertia of the reduced Hessian plus m positive and m negative eigenvalues. A positive-definite reduced Hessian therefore gives KKT inertia (n,m,0).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(Z^TGZ)+(m,m,0);\qquad Z^TGZ\succ0\Longrightarrow\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0).

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia Control by Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar primal regularization sufficient for the target KKT inertia.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_\delta=\begin{bmatrix}H+\delta I&A^{T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\). Its reduced Hessian is \[Z^{T}(H+\delta I)Z=Z^{T}HZ+\delta I.\] If \(\delta>-\lambda_{\min}(Z^{T}HZ)\), then \(Z^{T}(H+\delta I)Z\succ0\) and \(\operatorname{In}(K_\delta)=(n,m,0)\). If \(\delta=-\lambda_{\min}(Z^{T}HZ)\), then \(K_\delta\) is singular; if \(\delta<-\lambda_{\min}(Z^{T}HZ)\), then \(K_\delta\) has more than \(m\) negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar primal shift larger than the negative of the smallest reduced-Hessian eigenvalue produces the target nonsingular KKT inertia; equality produces singularity, and a smaller shift leaves negative reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\delta>-\lambda_{\min}(Z^{T}HZ)\), then \(\operatorname{In}(K_\delta)=(n,m,0)\).

If the null-space reduced matrix satisfies \(Z^TGZ\succ0\), conjugate gradients may instead be applied to the reduced system.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Krylov KKT Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned MINRES applied to a symmetric indefinite KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(y_0=P^{1/2}x_0\), \(B=P^{-1/2}KP^{-1/2}\), and \(c=P^{-1/2}b\). Apply MINRES to the symmetric system \(By=c\). At iteration \(j\), choose \(y_j\in y_0+\mathcal{K}_j(B,c-By_0)\) minimizing \(\lVert c-By_j\rVert_2\), and set \(x_j=P^{-1/2}y_j\). Stop at the first \(j\) satisfying \[\lVert b-Kx_j\rVert_{P^{-1}}\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_{P^{-1}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric positive-definite preconditioning preserves symmetry, allowing MINRES to minimize the preconditioned residual norm for a symmetric indefinite KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\), an initial iterate \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate satisfies \(\lVert b-Kx_j\rVert_{P^{-1}}\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_{P^{-1}}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric Krylov KKT Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-preconditioned GMRES for KKT systems whose preconditioning destroys symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply Arnoldi iteration to \(KM^{-1}\) with starting vector \(r_0=b-Kx_0\). At iteration \(j\), choose \(z_j\in\mathcal{K}_j(KM^{-1},r_0)\) minimizing \[\lVert r_0-KM^{-1}z_j\rVert_2,\] and set \(x_j=x_0+M^{-1}z_j\). Stop at the first \(j\) satisfying \[\lVert b-Kx_j\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right-preconditioned GMRES accommodates a nonsymmetric preconditioned KKT operator while minimizing the true residual over its Arnoldi search space.
assumptions_latex: \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\), an initial iterate \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned GMRES iterate satisfies \(\lVert b-Kx_j\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Diagonal Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-spectrum result for the ideal SPD block-diagonal KKT preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_D=\operatorname{diag}(H,S)\). The generalized eigenproblem \(Ku=\lambda P_Du\) has eigenvalue \(1\) with multiplicity \(n-m\), and its remaining eigenvalues are the roots of \(\lambda^2-\lambda-1=0\), each with multiplicity \(m\). Hence \[\sigma(P_D^{-1}K)=\left\{1,\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right\}.\] The ideal preconditioned spectrum is independent of the matrix dimension and coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact primal and Schur blocks, the ideal block-diagonal preconditioner gives three eigenvalues: one with multiplicity n minus m and each golden-ratio root with multiplicity m.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(P_D^{-1}K)=\left\{1,\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right\}\), with multiplicities \(n-m\), \(m\), and \(m\), respectively.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact spectrum of the ideally block-diagonally preconditioned saddle-point matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Triangular Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-polynomial result for an ideal lower triangular KKT preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P_L=\begin{bmatrix}H&0\\A&-S\end{bmatrix}\), the left-preconditioned operator is \[P_L^{-1}K=\begin{bmatrix}I&H^{-1}A^{T}\\0&I\end{bmatrix}.\] It satisfies \[(P_L^{-1}K-I)^2=0.\] Thus every eigenvalue equals \(1\), the minimal polynomial has degree at most two, and unrestarted GMRES with this exact left preconditioner terminates in at most two iterations in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ideal lower block-triangular preconditioner produces a unit upper-triangular operator whose minimal polynomial has degree at most two, giving two-step exact-arithmetic GMRES termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((P_L^{-1}K-I)^2=0\), so exact-arithmetic unrestarted GMRES terminates in at most two iterations.

notation.meaning: Constraint preconditioner preserving the off-diagonal blocks.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generalized spectral reduction of a constraint preconditioner to the nullspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nullspace spectral characterization for a constraint-preserving KKT preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matrix \(P_C\) is nonsingular because \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z^{T}GZ\succ0\). For any generalized eigenpair \(Ku=lambda P_Cu\) with \(lambda\ne1\), the constraint equation forces the primal component to lie in \(\ker A\). Writing it as \(Zq\) yields \[(Z^{T}HZ)q=lambda(Z^{T}GZ)q.\] Thus all nonunit eigenvalues are reduced-space generalized eigenvalues; the complementary generalized eigenspace and associated algebraic multiplicity occur at \(lambda=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner preserves the KKT constraint blocks, leaving only reduced-Hessian mismatch to determine nonunit eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Preconditioners

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced generalized-eigenvalue characterization is plausible and locally appropriate, but the statement leaves the algebraic multiplicity and possible overlap at eigenvalue one unspecified. An authoritative theorem locator is needed before selecting a precise version.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-equivalence requirement for an approximate Schur-complement block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\alpha S\preceq\widehat S\preceq\beta S\), then every nonzero \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\) satisfies \[\frac{1}{\beta}\le\frac{y^{T}Sy}{y^{T}\widehat Sy}\le\frac{1}{\alpha}.\] Hence \[\sigma(\widehat S^{-1}S)\subseteq[1/\beta,1/\alpha],\qquad \kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\widehat S^{-1}S)\le\frac{\beta}{\alpha},\] where \(\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}\) is the ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue. Size-independent bounds on \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) give a size-independent spectral condition-number bound for the preconditioned Schur operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral equivalence between an approximate and exact Schur complement bounds the eigenvalues and spectral condition number of the preconditioned Schur operator.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(S=AH^{-1}A^{T}\).
\(\widehat S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is symmetric positive definite.
There exist constants \(0<\alpha\le\beta\) such that \(\alpha S\preceq\widehat S\preceq\beta S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(\widehat S^{-1}S)\subseteq[1/\beta,1/\alpha]\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\widehat S^{-1}S)\le\beta/\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue of the preconditioned Schur operator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Loewner spectral equivalence implies eigenvalue and condition-number bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard block-diagonal augmented-Lagrangian preconditioner for an equality-constrained symmetric KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\). For \(\gamma>0\), an augmented-Lagrangian preconditioner is represented by \[P_\gamma=\begin{bmatrix}H+\gamma A^{\mathsf T}A&0\\0&\gamma^{-1}I_m\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(A\) has full row rank and \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), then \(H+\gamma A^{\mathsf T}A\) is positive definite, so applications of \(P_\gamma^{-1}\) reduce to one augmented primal solve and one scaled dual solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmenting the primal block by a constraint penalty yields a positive-definite primal solve and a simple scaled dual solve under standard KKT assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+\gamma A^{\mathsf T}A\succ0\), and \(P_\gamma\) is nonsingular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. Moreover, positivity on ker(A) does not imply H+gamma A^T A is positive definite for every gamma>0 when H can have negative curvature outside ker(A); the claim generally requires H positive semidefinite or a sufficiently large, source-supported augmentation parameter.

children.title: Primal Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices applied to primal variables within QP KKT systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal change of primal variables in a symmetric KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\), \(z=(x,\lambda)\), and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D_x\), set \(x=D_x\widehat x\) and \(S_x=\operatorname{diag}(D_x,I_m)\). The congruently scaled equations are \[S_x^{\mathsf T}KS_x\widehat z=S_x^{\mathsf T}b,\qquad S_x^{\mathsf T}KS_x=\begin{bmatrix}D_x^{\mathsf T}HD_x&D_x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}\\AD_x&-C\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(\widehat z=(\widehat x,\lambda)\) solves the scaled system, then \(z=S_x\widehat z\) solves the original system; symmetry and inertia are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal scaling changes variable units by a diagonal congruence, preserving symmetry, inertia, and equivalence after mapping the primal solution back.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Kz=b\) if and only if \(S_x^{\mathsf T}KS_x\widehat z=S_x^{\mathsf T}b\) with \(z=S_x\widehat z\).

notation.meaning: Block scaling acting only on primal variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The congruence transformation and solution recovery are standard and the representation fits the leaf, but no source is cited. The dimensions and domains of H, A, C, b, and the scaled vector should also be made explicit in a sourced version.

children.title: Dual Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices applied to multipliers within QP KKT systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal change of multiplier units in a symmetric KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\), \(z=(x,\lambda)\), and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D_\lambda\), set \(\lambda=D_\lambda\widehat\lambda\) and \(S_\lambda=\operatorname{diag}(I_n,D_\lambda)\). Then \[S_\lambda^{\mathsf T}KS_\lambda=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}D_\lambda\\D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A&-D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}CD_\lambda\end{bmatrix},\qquad S_\lambda^{\mathsf T}KS_\lambda\widehat z=S_\lambda^{\mathsf T}b.\] Recovering \(z=S_\lambda\widehat z\) gives the original solution. The congruence preserves symmetry, rank, and inertia, although residual components are rescaled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual scaling changes multiplier units through a diagonal congruence, preserving the exact KKT solution structure while changing residual magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Kz=b\) if and only if \(S_\lambda^{\mathsf T}KS_\lambda\widehat z=S_\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\) with \(z=S_\lambda\widehat z\).

notation.meaning: Block scaling acting only on multipliers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual congruence transformation is mathematically plausible and the representation kind fits the leaf, but no source is cited. A sourced version should explicitly introduce the dimensions and domains of H, A, C, b, and the scaled vector.

children.title: Coupled Primal-Dual Scaling
children.top_down_role: Coordination of primal-variable scales with multiplier scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Primal-Dual Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous diagonal congruence scaling of primal and dual KKT variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(D_\lambda\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular diagonal matrices, and define \(S=\operatorname{diag}(D_x,D_\lambda)\). For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\), the coupled scaling is \[\widehat K=S^{\mathsf T}KS=\begin{bmatrix}D_x^{\mathsf T}HD_x&D_x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}D_\lambda\\D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}AD_x&-D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}CD_\lambda\end{bmatrix},\qquad \widehat b=S^{\mathsf T}b.\] The systems \(Kz=b\) and \(\widehat K\widehat z=\widehat b\) are equivalent under \(z=S\widehat z\), and Sylvester's law preserves inertia.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled scaling simultaneously changes primal and multiplier units, preserving exact solvability and inertia through a block-diagonal congruence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Kz=b\Longleftrightarrow \widehat K\widehat z=\widehat b\) under \(z=S\widehat z\), with \(\operatorname{inertia}(\widehat K)=\operatorname{inertia}(K)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simultaneous block-diagonal congruence and inertia statement are standard, and representation is the appropriate kind, but the record has no citation. The domains of all KKT blocks and vectors should be explicit in the sourced statement.

children.title: KKT System Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Row, column, or block equilibration regimes for KKT linear systems.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT System Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative diagonal equilibration of symmetric KKT rows and columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric KKT matrix \(K\), tolerance \(\tau>0\), and iteration limit \(J\), initialize \(S_0=I\) and \(K_0=K\). For \(j=0,\ldots,J-1\), compute positive factors \(d_i^{(j)}=(\max_k |(K_j)_{ik}|)^{-1/2}\) for every nonzero row, set \(D_j=\operatorname{diag}(d_i^{(j)})\), \(K_{j+1}=D_jK_jD_j\), and \(S_{j+1}=S_jD_j\). Stop when all nonzero row maxima lie in \([1-\tau,1+\tau]\), or at \(J\). Output \(S=S_{j+1}\), \(S^{\mathsf T}KS\), and \(S^{\mathsf T}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated symmetric diagonal rescaling brings nonzero KKT row maxima toward one while retaining congruence equivalence with the original system.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is symmetric and has no structurally zero row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output system is \(S^{\mathsf T}KS\widehat z=S^{\mathsf T}b\), with recovered solution \(z=S\widehat z\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal equilibration update at iteration j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a specific equilibration algorithm and therefore requires a source supporting its update and stopping rule. The output index S_{j+1} is also ambiguous if the stopping test is applied before an update. Algorithm is nevertheless the correct content kind for this leaf.

children.title: Scaling-Induced Numerical Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits caused by extreme, inconsistent, or poorly conditioned scaling choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Numerical Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision limits of otherwise exact diagonal KKT scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_{n+m})\) be a nonsingular diagonal scaling and \(\widehat K=S^{\mathsf T}KS\). Exact equivalence can fail computationally when some product \(|s_iK_{ij}s_j|\) lies outside the normal floating-point interval \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), causing underflow, overflow, or loss of structural entries. Moreover, recovery \(z=S\widehat z\) amplifies componentwise absolute error by \(|s_i|\). Thus scaling is numerically unsafe when its dynamic range or the scaled entries exceed representable limits, even though \(S\) remains mathematically invertible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible scaling may still fail numerically through overflow, underflow, erased matrix entries, or amplified recovery errors when its dynamic range is excessive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|s_iK_{ij}s_j|\notin[\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\) for a relevant nonzero entry, reliable finite-precision equivalence is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: Smallest and largest positive normal floating-point numbers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, but no finite-precision source is supplied. Falling below the smallest positive normal number can produce a subnormal result rather than immediate underflow to zero, so the stated boundary and claimed consequences need a precise floating-point model and authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric quasi-definite regularization of a saddle-point KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\), choose \(\delta_p>0\) and \(\delta_d>0\) and form \[K_{\delta}=\begin{bmatrix}H+\delta_p I_n&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-(C+\delta_d I_m)\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(H\succeq0\) and \(C\succeq0\), then the leading block is positive definite and the trailing block is negative definite. Consequently \(K_\delta\) is symmetric quasi-definite and nonsingular for every \(A\). Solving \(K_\delta z=b\) perturbs both primal stationarity and dual feasibility equations, so the residual for the unregularized matrix \(K\) must be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and negative dual diagonal shifts make a semidefinite KKT matrix symmetric quasi-definite and nonsingular, at the cost of solving a perturbed system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_\delta\) is symmetric quasi-definite and nonsingular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regularized block signs do imply a symmetric quasi-definite, nonsingular matrix under the stated semidefiniteness and positive-shift assumptions. However, this nontrivial property has no cited source. Representation is a suitable kind for the regularization construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Constraint Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical removal of dependent equality constraints before a KKT solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and rank tolerance \(\tau>0\), compute a rank-revealing factorization of \(A^{\mathsf T}\) with permutation \(\Pi\), and select numerical rank \(r\) from the factorization's diagonal or singular values. Partition \(\Pi^{\mathsf T}(A,b)=((A_1,b_1),(A_2,b_2))\), where \(A_1\) contains \(r\) independent rows. Test whether \(A_2x=b_2\) is implied by \(A_1x=b_1\) to tolerance \(\tau\). Report inconsistency if not; otherwise solve the reduced KKT system using \(A_1x=b_1\), and reconstruct nonunique multipliers only under an explicit convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-revealing factorization separates independent constraints, detects inconsistent dependent rows, and supplies a reduced full-row-rank KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns either a numerical inconsistency certificate or a reduced constraint system with \(\operatorname{rank}(A_1)=r\).

notation.meaning: Numerical row rank of the constraint matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no source specifies the rank-revealing factorization, numerical-rank rule, implication test, or multiplier convention. The claimed numerical inconsistency certificate is also not defined as a verifiable output and requires source-supported detail.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement for KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement using a fixed approximate KKT factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Kz=b\), an initial approximation \(z_0\), tolerance \(\tau>0\), iteration limit \(J\), and a fixed computed factorization \(M\approx K\), repeat for \(j=0,\ldots,J-1\): compute \(r_j=b-Kz_j\) in working or higher precision; stop if \(\|r_j\|\le\tau(\|K\|\|z_j\|+\|b\|)\); approximately solve \(M d_j=r_j\); and set \(z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j\). Stop on stagnation or at \(J\). Output the last iterate together with its original-system residual and backward-error estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement repeatedly solves residual-correction equations with a fixed KKT factorization until a normwise residual test, stagnation, or an iteration limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(K\), \(b\), and the fixed factorization \(M\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an iterate \(z_j\) accompanied by \(r_j=b-Kz_j\) and a normwise stopping assessment.

notation.meaning: Matrix represented by the computed KKT factorization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes an appropriate iterative-refinement algorithm, but no authoritative source is cited. The precision model, correction-solve accuracy, norm, backward-error formula, and stagnation criterion must be tied to a specific supported variant.

children.title: KKT Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual-based evidence for computed solutions of QP KKT systems.

assumptions_latex: \(K\), \(b\), and \(\widehat z\) are available to the verifier.
A subordinate vector norm and its induced matrix norm are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\le\tau\) certifies \(\|b-K\widehat z\|\le\tau(\|K\|\|\widehat z\|+\|b\|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise verification certificate for a computed KKT solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed vector \(\widehat z\) for \(Kz=b\), define \(r=b-K\widehat z\) and, for a chosen vector norm and its induced matrix norm, \[\rho=\frac{\|r\|}{\|K\|\,\|\widehat z\|+\|b\|},\] with \(\rho=0\) when numerator and denominator both vanish. The tuple \((\widehat z,r,\rho)\) is a KKT residual certificate because a verifier can recompute the matrix-vector product and denominator. Acceptance at tolerance \(\tau\) certifies \(\|b-K\widehat z\|\le\tau(\|K\|\|\widehat z\|+\|b\|)\), but does not alone certify small forward error for ill-conditioned \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recomputable normalized KKT residual certifies satisfaction of a normwise residual tolerance, but not necessarily closeness to the exact solution.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Residual Certificates

children.title: Componentwise Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Component-sensitive residual assessment for heterogeneous KKT blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise verification of a computed KKT solution against scaled local residual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K\widehat z\approx b\), let \(r=b-K\widehat z\) and define the nonnegative scale vector \(d=|K|\,|\widehat z|+|b|\), with absolute values and inequalities interpreted componentwise. Given \(\tau\ge0\), the pair \((\widehat z,r)\) passes the componentwise residual certificate when \[|r_i|\le\tau d_i\quad\text{for every }i,\] using the convention that \(d_i=0\) requires \(r_i=0\). Equivalently, the maximum ratio over indices with \(d_i>0\) is at most \(\tau\), and every zero-denominator row has zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each residual component is compared with its own data-dependent scale, preventing large rows from masking inaccurate small rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|b-K\widehat z|\le\tau(|K|\,|\widehat z|+|b|)\) componentwise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise inequality, including its zero-denominator convention, is internally consistent and certificate is the correct content kind. No source is cited, however, so the interpretation and terminology require authoritative support.

children.title: Normwise Backward-Error Certificates
children.top_down_role: Norm-based backward-error assessment for computed KKT solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Normwise Backward-Error Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise backward error for a computed KKT linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K\widehat z\approx b\), fix a subordinate norm and define \[\eta=\frac{\|b-K\widehat z\|}{\|K\|\,\|\widehat z\|+\|b\|}.\] Except for the zero-denominator convention, \(\eta\) equals the smallest \(\varepsilon\ge0\) for which perturbations \(\Delta K\) and \(\Delta b\) exist satisfying \((K+\Delta K)\widehat z=b+\Delta b\), \(\|\Delta K\|\le\varepsilon\|K\|\), and \(\|\Delta b\|\le\varepsilon\|b\|\). Hence \(\eta\le\tau\) certifies that \(\widehat z\) exactly solves a nearby KKT linear system in the chosen norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized residual is the minimal relative normwise perturbation making the computed vector an exact solution of a nearby linear system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta\le\tau\) certifies admissible perturbations \(\Delta K,\Delta b\) of relative norm at most \(\tau\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact minimal-perturbation characterization is a nontrivial backward-error theorem and has no citation. Its validity must be supported for the precise vector norm, induced matrix norm, and simultaneous relative perturbation model used here. Certificate is the appropriate content kind.

children.title: Componentwise Backward-Error Certificates
children.top_down_role: Component-sensitive backward-error assessment across KKT equations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_{\mathrm{cw}}(\widehat z)=\inf\{\varepsilon\ge 0:\exists\,\Delta K,\Delta f,\ (K+\Delta K)\widehat z=f+\Delta f,\ |\Delta K|\le\varepsilon|K|,\ |\Delta f|\le\varepsilon|f|\}=\max_i\frac{|r_i|}{(|K||\widehat z|+|f|)_i}

notation.meaning: KKT matrix, right-hand side, and computed primal-dual vector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical componentwise backward error for a linear KKT system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-system certificate for a computed KKT primal-dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the KKT system \(Kz=f\), let \(r=f-K\widehat z\). Define \(0/0=0\) and \(a/0=+\infty\) for \(a>0\). The componentwise backward-error certificate is
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{cw}}(\widehat z)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\frac{|r_i|}{(|K||\widehat z|+|f|)_i}.
\]
Equivalently, it is the least \(\varepsilon\ge0\) for which perturbations exist satisfying \((K+\Delta K)\widehat z=f+\Delta f\), \(|\Delta K|\le\varepsilon|K|\), and \(|\Delta f|\le\varepsilon|f|\), with all inequalities interpreted componentwise. Thus the displayed scalar certifies exact solution of a nearby componentwise-relative KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate is the smallest componentwise relative perturbation of the KKT matrix and right-hand side that makes the computed vector an exact solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Backward-Error Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise backward-error formula and certificate role are mathematically appropriate, but no inspectable source or specific locator supports the equality with the perturbation infimum.

children.title: Certificate Interpretation Across Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dependence of certificate meaning on variable, multiplier, or matrix scaling.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_{\mathrm{cw}}(D_c^{-1}\widehat z;D_rKD_c,D_rf)=\eta_{\mathrm{cw}}(\widehat z;K,f)

notation.meaning: positive row and variable scaling matrices

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagonal-scaling invariance follows from the componentwise certificate formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of componentwise certificates under positive diagonal KKT scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K'=D_rKD_c\), \(f'=D_rf\), and \(\widehat y=D_c^{-1}\widehat z\), where \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are positive diagonal. Then \(f'-K'\widehat y=D_r(f-K\widehat z)\) and
\[
|K'||\widehat y|+|f'|=D_r\bigl(|K||\widehat z|+|f|\bigr).
\]
Consequently, \(\eta_{\mathrm{cw}}(\widehat y;K',f')=\eta_{\mathrm{cw}}(\widehat z;K,f)\). Hence a componentwise certificate has the same interpretation across such scaling regimes when the variables are transformed consistently. A normwise residual or backward error need not share this invariance and must be interpreted together with the chosen scaling and norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistent positive diagonal row and variable scaling leaves componentwise backward error unchanged, whereas normwise measures can change with the scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Interpretation Across Scaling Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-diagonal scaling calculation is internally consistent and the property kind fits, but the invariance claim and comparison with normwise measures lack cited support.

children.title: Misleading Certificate Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where apparently small certificates do not establish adequate numerical reliability.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_\varepsilon\to0\quad\text{while}\quad \|\widehat z-z_\varepsilon^*\|_2/\|z_\varepsilon^*\|_2=1/\sqrt2
review_flags: source requested for contextual interpretation as a KKT certificate boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete conditioning boundary for residual-based numerical certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), consider \(K_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\), \(f_\varepsilon=(1,\varepsilon)^T\), and \(\widehat z=(1,0)^T\). The exact solution is \(z_\varepsilon^*=(1,1)^T\), while the residual is \(r_\varepsilon=f_\varepsilon-K_\varepsilon\widehat z=(0,\varepsilon)^T\). Therefore the relative residual
\[
\rho_\varepsilon=\frac{\|r_\varepsilon\|_2}{\|K_\varepsilon\|_2\|\widehat z\|_2+\|f_\varepsilon\|_2}
\]
tends to zero, but \(\|\widehat z-z_\varepsilon^*\|_2/\|z_\varepsilon^*\|_2=1/\sqrt2\). Thus a small residual or backward error alone does not certify small forward error when the KKT system becomes ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ill-conditioned diagonal family has residuals tending to zero while its computed solutions retain a fixed relative forward error.
knowledge_statements.title: Misleading Certificate Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit diagonal counterfamily is correct and demonstrates the stated conditioning boundary, but no source supports its interpretation as a KKT certificate failure boundary.

children.title: Quadratic Subproblem Solver Tradeoff Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Accuracy and structural selection regimes specific to quadratic subproblem solvers; general optimization complexity and global nonconvex-QP hardness remain outside this chapter.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Conn, Gould, and Toint, Trust Region Methods
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Conn, Gould, and Toint, Trust Region Methods

children.title: Exact Subproblem Solve Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quadratic subproblem settings where exact solution is the operative accuracy target.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x\in\arg\min_{x\in P}q(x)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact solution of a convex quadratic program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical exactness, distinct from exact arithmetic in an implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the convex quadratic subproblem
\[
\min_{x\in P}q(x),\qquad q(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+g^Tx,
\]
where \(Q=Q^T\succeq0\) and \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\ge d\}\) is nonempty. An exact subproblem solve returns \(\widehat x\in P\) satisfying \(q(\widehat x)=\inf_{x\in P}q(x)\). Equivalently, when a KKT constraint qualification holds, it returns multipliers for which primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity hold with zero residual. The regime concerns exact satisfaction of the mathematical optimality conditions; it does not require every internal arithmetic operation to be exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact regime returns a global minimizer of the convex quadratic subproblem, equivalently a zero-residual KKT point under a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Subproblem Solve Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes mathematical optimality from exact internal arithmetic, but the global-minimizer and KKT-equivalence characterization has no authoritative convex-QP citation.

children.title: Nearly Exact Subproblem Solve Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quadratic subproblem settings using accuracy close to exact solution.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r_p\|\le\tau_p,\quad\|r_d\|\le\tau_d,\quad\|r_c\|\le\tau_c,\quad q(\widehat x)-d(\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\le\tau_g

notation.meaning: primal, dual, and complementarity KKT residuals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tolerance-based approximate KKT and gap criterion
normalization and solver-specific tolerance source required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-defined near-exactness for convex quadratic subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex quadratic subproblem and a primal-dual candidate \((\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\) with \(\widehat\lambda\ge0\), a nearly exact regime accepts the candidate only if
\[
\|r_p\|\le\tau_p,
\qquad \|r_d\|\le\tau_d,
\qquad \|r_c\|\le\tau_c,
\qquad 0\le q(\widehat x)-d(\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\le\tau_g,
\]
where the residuals represent primal feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity. Each tolerance is measured in a declared absolute or relative scaling. Exactness is approached when all four tolerances tend to zero; without fixed norms and scaling conventions, the phrase nearly exact does not define a reproducible regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearly exact solve meets declared small tolerances for primal feasibility, stationarity, complementarity, and primal-dual gap under fixed scaling conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Exact Subproblem Solve Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the residuals and absolute-relative scaling rules are not defined precisely enough to identify a reproducible nearly-exact regime, and no solver or textbook source supplies those conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Acceptance Conditions for a Nearly Exact Trust-Region Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-fraction model-decrease and radius-multiple conditions for accepting an approximate trust-region subproblem solution, including their negative-curvature significance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
m(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp,
\]
let \(p^*\) be an exact minimizer of the trust-region subproblem over \(\|p\|\le\Delta\), and choose constants \(c_1\in(0,1]\) and \(\gamma>0\). The approximate step \(p\) is required to satisfy
\[
m(0)-m(p)\ge c_1\bigl(m(0)-m(p^*)\bigr),\qquad \|p\|\le\gamma\Delta.
\]
The first condition guarantees a fixed fraction of the maximum model decrease. If \(g=0\) and \(B\) has a negative eigenvalue, then \(m(0)-m(p^*)>0\), so the condition remains nonvacuous and requires positive model decrease despite the zero gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted nearly exact step must attain a fixed fraction of the best trust-region model decrease and have norm at most a fixed multiple of the radius. Unlike a bound based only on the gradient, the decrease condition remains effective at a zero-gradient point with negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m(0)-m(p)\ge c_1\bigl(m(0)-m(p^*)\bigr)\quad\land\quad\|p\|\le\gamma\Delta

children.title: Exactness Transition Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria separating exact-solve expectations from nearly exact accuracy targets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\widehat x)=d(\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\iff (\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\text{ is primal-dual optimal}
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: zero primal-dual gap under strong duality
authoritative convex QP duality source required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition from tolerance-based acceptance to exact convex-QP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the convex quadratic subproblem has strong duality. For any primal-feasible \(\widehat x\) and dual-feasible \((\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\), weak duality gives
\[
G=q(\widehat x)-d(\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\ge0.
\]
The solve crosses from a nearly exact regime to mathematical exactness precisely when \(G=0\): then both feasible points attain the common primal and dual optimum and satisfy the KKT conditions. In a numerical implementation, testing \(G\le\tau_g\) with \(\tau_g>0\) remains a nearly exact criterion; it becomes an exactness criterion only when zero is established in the adopted arithmetic or by a separate exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong duality, a feasible primal-dual pair becomes exactly optimal when its gap is proven zero; any positive tolerance defines only near exactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Transition Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Zero gap for a primal- and dual-feasible pair correctly implies optimality, but the dual objective, feasibility convention, and asserted KKT consequence require a specific convex-QP duality source.

children.title: High-Accuracy Solver Consequences
children.top_down_role: Computational consequences of imposing exact or nearly exact subproblem accuracy.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat x-x^*\|_2\le\|r\|_2/\mu,\qquad 0\le q(\widehat x)-q(x^*)\le\|r\|_2^2/(2\mu)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual-to-solution and residual-to-objective bounds for a strongly convex quadratic
source required for the selected unconstrained specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained strongly convex quadratic specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+g^Tx\) with \(Q=Q^T\succeq\mu I\) and \(\mu>0\). Its unique minimizer is \(x^*=-Q^{-1}g\). For any computed \(\widehat x\), let \(r=Q\widehat x+g\). Then
\[
\|\widehat x-x^*\|_2\le\frac{\|r\|_2}{\mu},
\qquad
0\le q(\widehat x)-q(x^*)
=\tfrac12r^TQ^{-1}r
\le\frac{\|r\|_2^2}{2\mu}.
\]
Thus a high-accuracy stationarity solve yields a linear forward-solution bound and a quadratic objective-gap bound, with constants controlled by the smallest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strongly convex quadratic, a small stationarity residual bounds solution error linearly and objective error quadratically, scaled by inverse curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: High-Accuracy Solver Consequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unconstrained strongly convex quadratic identities and bounds are correct, and property is an appropriate kind, but the selected specialization has no cited theorem or section locator.

children.title: Finite-Precision Accuracy Limits
children.top_down_role: Numerical boundaries restricting attainable subproblem accuracy.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\|\widehat z-z\|}{\|z\|}\le\frac{\kappa(K)}{1-\kappa(K)\delta_K}(\delta_K+\delta_f)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical normwise perturbation bound for linear systems
exact numerical linear algebra theorem locator required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning barrier for finite-precision KKT linear solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Kz=f\) be nonsingular, and suppose a computed solution satisfies \((K+\Delta K)\widehat z=f+\Delta f\). With \(\delta_K=\|\Delta K\|/\|K\|\), \(\delta_f=\|\Delta f\|/\|f\|\), and \(\kappa(K)\delta_K<1\),
\[
\frac{\|\widehat z-z\|}{\|z\|}
\le
\frac{\kappa(K)}{1-\kappa(K)\delta_K}(\delta_K+\delta_f).
\]
A backward-stable finite-precision method typically has perturbations of order \(u\), so useful forward accuracy requires \(\kappa(K)u\ll1\). When \(\kappa(K)u\) approaches one, increasing iterations without higher precision, refinement, or better conditioning cannot generally guarantee additional correct digits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward stability yields forward accuracy only when condition number times unit roundoff is small; near that boundary, tighter iteration tolerances cannot ensure more digits.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Accuracy Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed normwise perturbation bound is standard under the stated induced-norm assumptions, but it lacks a theorem locator; the claims about order-u perturbations and iteration limits also depend on the particular algorithm and stability constants.

review_flags: solver-independent normalization requires authoritative source or local convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent definition using scaled approximate KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An inexact solve of a convex quadratic subproblem returns a primal-dual candidate before all KKT residuals vanish. Fix positive scales \(s_p,s_d,s_c,s_g\), each combining a declared absolute tolerance with a relative data-dependent tolerance. The candidate is acceptable when
\[
\max\left\{
\frac{\|r_p\|}{s_p},
\frac{\|r_d\|}{s_d},
\frac{\|r_c\|}{s_c},
\frac{G}{s_g}
\right\}\le1,
\]
where \(G\ge0\) is the primal-dual gap for a feasible pair. The regime is defined by the complete residual vector, norms, and scales, rather than by iteration count alone. Positive tolerances distinguish it from an exact solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact solve is accepted when declared scaled primal, stationarity, complementarity, and gap measures all meet positive tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subproblem Solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is suitable for this regime container, but the residuals and scales are only described abstractly and no authoritative or declared local convention establishes this solver-independent acceptance test.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le q(\widehat x)-q(x^*)\le G=q(\widehat x)-d(\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weak-duality early-termination certificate for convex QP
source required for broader certificate-family taxonomy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-QP primal-dual gap as a representative early-termination family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex quadratic program, let \(\widehat x\) be primal feasible and \((\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)\) dual feasible. The computable gap
\[
G=q(\widehat x)-d(\widehat y,\widehat\lambda)
\]
is nonnegative and, for every primal optimum \(x^*\), satisfies \(0\le q(\widehat x)-q(x^*)\le G\). Hence \(G\le\tau_g\) certifies early termination with objective suboptimality at most \(\tau_g\). Other valid early-termination families certify scaled KKT residuals, a trust-region model decrease, or detected negative curvature; each must state the precise quantity bounded and the assumptions connecting that quantity to the required outer-solver guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal-dual pair with gap at most the tolerance certifies that early termination loses at most that tolerance in objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Early-Termination Certificate Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-dual-gap certificate follows from weak duality and fits the certificate kind, but the broader claims about residual, model-decrease, and negative-curvature certificate families lack precise assumptions and cited support.

assumptions_latex: \text{each nonoptimal iteration changes the working set without cycling}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{the active-set method terminates after finitely many working-set changes at the unique minimizer}

notation.meaning: current subset of active inequality constraints

review_flags: method version is underspecified by the node title
finite-termination theorem requires an authoritative active-set algorithm locator
anti-cycling and nondegeneracy variants need review
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic feasible active-set regime with an anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a feasible active-set method for minimizing \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+g^Tx\) over a nonempty polyhedron \(P\), with \(Q=Q^T\succ0\). Assume exact arithmetic; each equality-constrained working-set subproblem is solved exactly; a blocking constraint or a constraint with an inadmissible multiplier is updated according to a deterministic anti-cycling rule; and no nonoptimal iteration repeats a working set with the same iterate. Because only finitely many working sets exist, the method performs finitely many changes. It terminates at a feasible point satisfying the KKT conditions, which is the unique global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex feasible active-set method terminates finitely in exact arithmetic when subproblems are exact and its update rule prevents cycling.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Termination Active-Set Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits, but the active-set algorithm and anti-cycling mechanism are not specified. Finitely many working sets plus the stated prohibition on repeating the same working set with the same iterate does not itself exclude revisiting a working set at a different iterate, so an authoritative algorithm-specific theorem is required.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|e_k\|_H\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|e_0\|_H

notation.meaning: symmetric positive-definite reduced Hessian or preconditioned operator

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical conjugate-gradient energy-norm convergence bound
indefinite KKT variants are outside this specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate gradients on an SPD reduced or preconditioned quadratic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Apply exact-arithmetic conjugate gradients to \(Hx=b\), where \(H=H^T\succ0\), and write \(e_k=x_k-x^*\) and \(\kappa=\lambda_{\max}(H)/\lambda_{\min}(H)\). Then
\[
\|e_k\|_H\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|e_0\|_H.
\]
For \(\kappa>1\), relative energy error at most \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\) is therefore guaranteed once
\[
k\ge\frac{\log(2/\epsilon)}{\log((\sqrt\kappa+1)/(\sqrt\kappa-1))}.
\]
Each iteration uses one operator product, so this is also a matrix-vector-product bound. For \(\kappa=1\), one iteration suffices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate gradients reduce SPD energy error geometrically at a condition-number-controlled rate, giving a matching matrix-vector-product complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Iteration-Complexity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-arithmetic conjugate-gradient energy-norm and iteration bounds are correct for an SPD operator, and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but no authoritative Krylov theorem locator is supplied.

children.title: Factorization Arithmetic Cost Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operation-cost regimes for factorizations used in quadratic subproblem linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Arithmetic Cost Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic bounds for sparse Cholesky factorization under a fixed elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), fix a symmetric permutation \(P\), and let \(PAP^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\). If \(d_j\) is the number of subdiagonal nonzeros in column \(j\) of \(L\), then a column-oriented factorization requires \(\Theta\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^n(d_j+1)^2\right)\) arithmetic operations, up to implementation-dependent constants. Thus the dense regime \(d_j=\Theta(n-j)\) costs \(\Theta(n^3)\), while uniformly bounded column counts \(d_j=O(1)\) give \(O(n)\) arithmetic. Intermediate sparse regimes are governed by the entire elimination profile, not merely by \(\operatorname{nnz}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization work is the sum of squared filled-column sizes: cubic for dense factors, linear for uniformly bounded columns, and profile-dependent between those extremes.
assumptions_latex: The permutation \(P\) and resulting Cholesky sparsity pattern are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{work}(A,P)=\Theta\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^n(d_j+1)^2\right)\).

notation.meaning: Number of subdiagonal nonzeros in column j of the Cholesky factor.
Number of stored nonzero entries of A.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the terminal container, and the stated elimination-profile regimes are mathematically plausible. However, no inspectable source supports the exact Theta bound or its implementation model, so source uncertainty prevents acceptance.

children.title: Sparse Factorization Fill Regimes
children.top_down_role: Fill behavior across sparse KKT or reduced-system factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Factorization Fill Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph characterization of symbolic fill for symmetric positive-definite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) have undirected sparsity graph \(G(A)\), and fix an elimination ordering \(\pi\). Symbolic Cholesky elimination repeatedly makes the uneliminated neighbors of the current vertex a clique and then removes that vertex. The resulting chordal completion \(G_\pi^+\) is the sparsity graph of \(L+L^{\mathsf T}\) for \(P_\pi A P_\pi^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\), absent numerical cancellation. Consequently, \(\operatorname{nnz}(L)\) equals \(n\) plus the number of oriented edges in \(G_\pi^+\); low-fill and high-fill regimes correspond respectively to sparse and dense completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cholesky fill is determined by the chordal completion induced by the elimination ordering; sparse or dense completions produce low- or high-memory factorization regimes.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) has a structurally symmetric sparsity pattern.
Numerical cancellation is excluded when identifying symbolic and numerical patterns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(L+L^{\mathsf T})=G_\pi^+\) and \(\operatorname{nnz}(L)=n+|E(G_\pi^+)|\).

notation.meaning: Chordal completion generated by ordering pi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the graph-based fill characterization. The symbolic-completion identity and nonzero-count formula require an authoritative sparse-factorization source with a specific locator.

children.title: Ordering Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of factorization cost or fill on permutation choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of sparse-factor storage and arithmetic on the elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed matrix \(A\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), two symmetric permutations \(P_\pi\) and \(P_\sigma\) can induce different chordal completions and hence different factorization resources. If \(P_\tau A P_\tau^{\mathsf T}=L_\tau L_\tau^{\mathsf T}\) and \(d_j^\tau\) counts subdiagonal entries in column \(j\) of \(L_\tau\), then storage is proportional to \(n+\sum_j d_j^\tau\), whereas arithmetic is proportional to \(\sum_j(d_j^\tau+1)^2\). Therefore equal input sparsity does not imply equal factorization cost: changing only \(\tau\) may alter both quantities substantially.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse direct-solver cost depends on ordering because different permutations create different fill, changing both factor storage and arithmetic work.
assumptions_latex: Each factorization uses symmetric permutation and symbolic fill without numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\neq\sigma\) may yield \(\operatorname{nnz}(L_\pi)\neq\operatorname{nnz}(L_\sigma)\) and unequal factorization work.

notation.meaning: Cholesky factor produced under ordering tau.
Subdiagonal nonzero count in column j under ordering tau.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind matches Ordering Sensitivity, and the claim is standard. No cited evidence supports the storage and arithmetic formulas or the asserted ordering dependence.

children.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse opportunities when sparsity structure persists across related subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse criterion for repeated sparse factorizations with invariant structural pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider matrices \(A_k\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) whose structural sparsity graphs are identical, and fix one permutation \(P\). The elimination tree, column structure, and storage addresses of the symbolic Cholesky factor of \(PA_kP^{\mathsf T}\) are then independent of \(k\), provided structural nonzeros remain represented and numerical pivoting is unnecessary. Hence symbolic analysis may be performed once and reused for every \(k\); only numerical factorization and triangular solves must be repeated. A change of sparsity pattern, ordering, or pivot sequence invalidates this reuse guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated matrices with one fixed sparsity pattern and ordering can share symbolic analysis; pattern changes or numerical pivoting can invalidate that reuse.
assumptions_latex: The symmetric permutation \(P\) is fixed and factorization requires no numerical pivoting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symbolic factor pattern and elimination tree are computed once and reused across all \(k\).

notation.meaning: Matrix in a repeated factorization sequence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the reuse criterion, and the qualifications concerning fixed structure, ordering, and pivoting are appropriate. An inspectable source is still required for the symbolic-reuse guarantee.

children.title: Memory-Limited Factorization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where fill-driven storage demands restrict direct factorization.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Limited Factorization Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage feasibility boundary for explicit sparse direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), let ordering \(\pi\) produce Cholesky factor \(L_\pi\), and suppose available factor-storage capacity is \(M\) scalar words. Explicit factorization is storage-feasible only if \(\operatorname{nnz}(L_\pi)+W_\pi\le M\), where \(W_\pi\) is the peak auxiliary workspace measured in scalar words. If this inequality fails, an in-core implementation cannot complete regardless of arithmetic speed. Reordering can move the boundary by reducing fill; otherwise feasibility requires an out-of-core or compressed method, or replacement by an iterative matrix-free solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An in-core factorization fails when factor entries plus peak workspace exceed available memory; reordering or a different storage/solver architecture is then required.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(W_\pi\) use the same scalar-word accounting convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}(L_\pi)+W_\pi>M\) excludes in-core explicit factorization.

notation.meaning: Available storage capacity in scalar words.
Peak auxiliary workspace under ordering pi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container. The boundary depends on an implementation-specific memory-accounting model, and no source establishes that factor entries plus the stated workspace exhaust the relevant in-core storage requirement.

assumptions_latex: \(m\ll n\), applications of \(H^{-1}\) are computationally available, and forming or applying the Schur complement is affordable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solve \(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-(b+AH^{-1}g)\), then recover \(x=-H^{-1}(g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range-space reduction criterion for equality-constrained convex quadratic subproblems.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(m\le n\). Consider minimizing \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(H\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Eliminating \(x\) from the KKT equations gives the positive-definite range-space system \((AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})\lambda=-(b+AH^{-1}g)\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\), followed by \(x=-H^{-1}(g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda)\). This regime is structurally appropriate when \(m\ll n\), applications of \(H^{-1}\) are available, and forming or applying the \(m\times m\) Schur complement is affordable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex equality-constrained quadratic problem with few independent constraints and efficient Hessian solves, eliminate the primal variables, solve the smaller positive-definite range-space system for the multipliers, and recover the primal solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Few-Constraint Range-Space Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ax_p=b\).
The columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique minimizer is \(x=x_p+Zp\), where \((Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p=-Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\).

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns form a basis for the null space of A.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction criterion for equality-constrained quadratic subproblems with low nullity.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(m\le n\). Consider minimizing \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(H\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Let \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(Ax_p=b\), and let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Every feasible point has the unique representation \(x=x_p+Zp\) with \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\), and stationarity reduces to \((Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p=-Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\). The null-space regime is appropriate when \(n-m\ll n\), a usable basis \(Z\) is available, and \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{n-m}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-constrained quadratic problem whose feasible null space is low-dimensional, parameterize every feasible point with a null-space basis and solve the positive-definite reduced-Hessian system for the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Few-Free-Variable Null-Space Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Started Active-Set Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural regime favoring reuse of a nearby active set in sequential quadratic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence of convex quadratic programs with slowly changing data, let \(\mathcal{W}_{k-1}\) be the working set returned for problem \(k-1\). A warm-started active-set method is appropriate when \(\mathcal{W}_{k-1}\) is primal-feasible or cheaply repairable for problem \(k\), the optimal active set \(\mathcal{A}_k^*\) differs from it by few indices, and KKT factorizations admit efficient updates. Initialize \(\mathcal{W}_k=\mathcal{W}_{k-1}\), solve the equality-constrained subproblem, and add or delete constraints until primal feasibility and multiplier sign conditions hold; those conditions certify optimality for the convex problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set warm starts are favorable when consecutive convex QPs have nearly identical active constraints and their KKT factorizations can be updated cheaply.
assumptions_latex: Each quadratic program is convex and has linear constraints.
The preceding working set is feasible or cheaply repairable.
Successive optimal active sets differ by few constraint indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal{W}_k=\mathcal{W}_{k-1}\) and terminate when primal feasibility and the required multiplier signs hold.

notation.meaning: Working set used for problem k.
Optimal active-constraint set for problem k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the regime container, but the constraint form and multiplier sign convention are not specified, so the claimed optimality certificate is not fully checkable. An authoritative active-set warm-start source is also absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Scale Matrix-Free Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection boundary for iterative quadratic solvers using operator products instead of explicit matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a quadratic subproblem in \(n\) variables whose solver needs products with the Hessian \(H\), constraint operators \(A\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\), and a preconditioner \(M^{-1}\). A matrix-free Krylov architecture is appropriate when these products can be computed without storing the matrices, their combined cost and storage are acceptable, and explicit factor storage would exceed the memory budget. Iteration may stop when the relevant residual satisfies \(\|r_k\|\le\varepsilon\|r_0\|\). Its memory is then \(O(nq)\) scalar words for \(q\) retained vectors, apart from operator and preconditioner state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a matrix-free Krylov solver when operator products and preconditioning are available but explicit matrices or factors are too large to store.
assumptions_latex: Required products with \(H\), \(A\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}\) are available as operators.
A suitable preconditioner action \(M^{-1}\) is available.
Explicit factor storage exceeds the prescribed memory budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An iterative solve can use \(O(nq)\) vector storage and terminate at \(\|r_k\|\le\varepsilon\|r_0\|\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the solver-selection leaf, but no particular Krylov system or recurrence is specified. For constrained saddle-point systems, retained vectors may have dimension n+m rather than n, so the stated O(nq) storage bound is not reliable without a solver-specific formulation and source.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Direct Repeated-Solve Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection boundary for amortizing sparse symbolic analysis or numerical factorization across repeated solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_tz_t=r_t\) be a sequence of sparse linear systems arising from quadratic subproblems. A sparse-direct repeated-solve architecture is appropriate when every \(K_t\) has the same structural pattern and ordering, factor storage fits memory, and either the numerical matrix is constant or changes infrequently. For a constant \(K\), perform symbolic analysis and numerical factorization once, then solve each right-hand side by two triangular substitutions. If numerical values change while the pattern remains fixed, reuse symbolic analysis but refactor numerically. The setup cost is amortized when sufficiently many solves share each factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated sparse systems favor direct solution when factor memory fits and many right-hand sides or value updates can reuse symbolic analysis or a numerical factor.
assumptions_latex: All \(K_t\) share one structural sparsity pattern and ordering.
The sparse factors and workspace fit available memory.
Each unchanged numerical factor is used for multiple right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse symbolic analysis across \(t\), and reuse the numerical factor whenever \(K_t\) itself is unchanged.

notation.meaning: Sparse KKT or reduced-system matrix at solve t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the repeated-solve regime. For possibly indefinite KKT matrices, fixed structural pattern and ordering do not alone guarantee reusable numerical factor structure because pivoting may vary; the amortization claim also lacks a quantitative or sourced cost model.
